Speedup is the device count times the compute share of each update; training time and cost follow from the one-device run.



engine.solvers.parallelism.ParallelLayoutModel()
One training step of a TP x PP x DP layout, read through the Fleet Law.
Compute: the step’s 6 P D FLOPs (flops_per_param_token per parameter per token, D tokens per update) spread over every device at a local share of peak. Communication: each data-parallel rank reduces its gradient shard (the full gradient over TP x PP) with a ring AllReduce of about twice the shard; up to overlap_fraction of that transfer hides under the compute window, never more than the window itself. Pipeline stages idle (p-1)/(m+p-1) of the step, which stretches the compute window by 1/(1 - bubble). State: 16 B per parameter of mixed-precision Adam split over TP x PP; ZeRO-1 also shards the 12 B of optimizer state across the data-parallel group.
Literature Source: 1. Narayanan et al. (2021), Megatron-LM 3D parallelism. 2. Rajbhandari et al. (2020), ZeRO (16 B/param, optimizer sharding). 3. Huang et al. (2019), GPipe (bubble fraction).



engine.solvers.parallelism.TensorParallelLayerModel()
One Transformer layer’s forward compute against its tensor-parallel exchange.
The layer’s forward pass is 2 (P/L) FLOPs per token, split over the TP group and run at a sustained share of peak. Megatron-style tensor parallelism sums an activation of tokens x d_model once after attention and once after the MLP, each a ring AllReduce of 2(t-1)/t times the payload per device. The exchange must fit inside the compute on the link that carries it.
Literature Source: 1. Shoeybi et al. (2019), “Megatron-LM” (two AllReduces per layer per pass).



engine.solvers.parallelism.ZeroShardingModel()
Per-device training state at each ZeRO stage, and what full sharding sends.
DDP replicates weights (W), gradients (G), and optimizer state (O) on every device. ZeRO-1 shards O over N devices, ZeRO-2 also G, and ZeRO-3 (FSDP) also W. Stages 1 and 2 move DDP’s bytes (a ring AllReduce, about 2W per device); ZeRO-3 gathers every layer’s weights in forward and again in backward and reduce-scatters the gradients, about 3W, 1.5x as much.
Literature Source: 1. Rajbhandari et al. (2020), “ZeRO” (stages and communication volume).

title: engine.solvers.cost_accounting
text:
engine.solvers.cost_accounting
Agent cost-accounting solvers: what one accepted task costs, and what each lever buys (added 2026-10-20).
Domain implementations behind mlsysim.solvers. Each model is arithmetic on stated inputs: the fitted fall of a fixed capability’s price, cost against score on long-horizon trials, a cohort of one-attempt tasks under a tariff, prefix-cache bills and the payback of one compaction, retry policies under independent attempts, a serial episode under Amdahl’s law and speculative decoding, a tiered model cascade under one gate, admission against a token quota, Kingman’s queue price, renting tokens against owning capacity, a conserved budget across children, architectures with a human fallback, the payback of a one-time adaptation, per-workload levers on cost per accepted task, measured coverage against independent trials, and one server swept across concurrency. None models a particular provider’s billing system.





Name
Description




AdaptationPaybackModel
Tasks until a one-time adaptation repays its data, training, and evaluation.


ArchitectureChoiceModel
Designs priced by automated spend alone and with a human fallback.


CohortAttemptCostModel
One configuration’s cohort: one bounded attempt per task, all charges settled.


CompactionPaybackModel
One compaction priced against keeping the transcript, under one tariff.


ConservedBudgetModel
A root budget kept as settled + reserved + free across two children.


DedicatedBreakEvenModel
Renting tokens from an API against owning capacity with a fixed hourly cost.


KingmanQueueModel
Kingman’s mean wait for one server at two utilizations, and its holding price.


ModelCascadeModel
A tiered cascade under one acceptance gate, priced over a completed cohort.


PrefixCacheBillModel
An append-only trajectory billed at the fresh rate, and with ideal prefix reuse.


RetryPolicyModel
Bounded attempt policies under independent attempts at a fixed all-in cost.


SerialEpisodeModel
One serial episode of disjoint intervals; a faster model shortens only its own.


SpeculativeEpisodeModel
Speculative decoding’s decode-stream speedup, composed with a serial episode.


TrajectoryAdmissionModel
Admitted trajectories against a token quota, in the mean.


WorkloadLeverModel
Cost per accepted task by workload, C_eff = C_attempt / p_acc, and three levers.





engine.solvers.cost_accounting.AdaptationPaybackModel()
Tasks until a one-time adaptation repays its data, training, and evaluation.
Each task’s model usage is steps times (input tokens x input price + output tokens x output price); the break-even count is the investment over the per-task saving, and the first whole task that crosses it.



engine.solvers.cost_accounting.ArchitectureChoiceModel()
Designs priced by automated spend alone and with a human fallback.
A bounded loop stops at its first accepted turn, so turn j is reached by the share that every earlier turn rejected. Rejected tickets go to a person who resolves a fraction of them; cost per resolved ticket divides the combined spend by combined resolution.



engine.solvers.cost_accounting.CohortAttemptCostModel()
One configuration’s cohort: one bounded attempt per task, all charges settled.
The attempt costs its turns of model tokens and environment plus one assessment; the cohort cost per accepted task divides every attempt’s cost by the accepted count, and triage charges each rejected attempt.



engine.solvers.cost_accounting.CompactionPaybackModel()
One compaction priced against keeping the transcript, under one tariff.
Compacting at call n_c replaces S tokens of context with a S_c-token summary that costs K output tokens and is resent fresh, so the compacting call costs p_out K + p_in S_c more; every later call reads S - S_c fewer cached tokens. Compaction has paid after n* = 1 + ceil(upfront / per-call saving) calls.



engine.solvers.cost_accounting.ConservedBudgetModel()
A root budget kept as settled + reserved + free across two children.
Granting moves free to reserved; a child that closes settles its charge and returns the rest. A child stopped with a remote operation pending keeps that operation’s enforceable bound reserved until its final bill settles, once per settlement identity however often it is delivered.



engine.solvers.cost_accounting.DedicatedBreakEvenModel()
Renting tokens from an API against owning capacity with a fixed hourly cost.
The API’s price per output token carries its input mix; owning pays a fixed F per hour plus v per output token. The costs tie at load u* = F / (3600 R (P_eff - v)) of the reference rate R.



engine.solvers.cost_accounting.KingmanQueueModel()
Kingman’s mean wait for one server at two utilizations, and its holding price.
E[W] = (c_a^2 + c_s^2) / 2 * rho / (1 - rho) * E[S]; each second of wait holds resources at holding_rate dollars.



engine.solvers.cost_accounting.ModelCascadeModel()
A tiered cascade under one acceptance gate, priced over a completed cohort.
Every reached tier pays its call and the gate; the cascade’s cost per accepted task divides the whole spend by every tier’s exits. Optionally a harm per false accept at the first tier, whose break-even rate erases the cascade’s saving over the top tier alone.



engine.solvers.cost_accounting.PrefixCacheBillModel()
An append-only trajectory billed at the fresh rate, and with ideal prefix reuse.
The logical input is H s0 + delta H (H - 1) / 2; ideal reuse bills only s0 + (H - 1) delta at the input rate and the rest at the cached rate, so caching scales the quadratic term down without removing it. A miss on miss_fraction of the eligible prefix bills it at the full rate.



engine.solvers.cost_accounting.RetryPolicyModel()
Bounded attempt policies under independent attempts at a fixed all-in cost.
Sequential retry with early stopping covers 1 - (1 - p)^k of tasks in coverage / p attempts on average, so its cost per accepted task is c / p whatever the cap; a batch of k pays for all k.



engine.solvers.cost_accounting.SerialEpisodeModel()
One serial episode of disjoint intervals; a faster model shortens only its own.
T' = T_other + T_model / s (Amdahl’s law); instant model calls bound the episode speedup at 1 / (1 - f).



engine.solvers.cost_accounting.SpeculativeEpisodeModel()
Speculative decoding’s decode-stream speedup, composed with a serial episode.
Treats the episode’s model time as pure decode (an optimistic bound): T' = T [(1 - f) + f / S] with S = (m + 1) / (gamma r + 1).



engine.solvers.cost_accounting.TrajectoryAdmissionModel()
Admitted trajectories against a token quota, in the mean.
Little’s law gives the trajectories present; the call and token rates scale with admissions. At fixed goodput, admissions scale as 1 / alpha, so a relative acceptance drop of 1 - quota_share fills the quota.



engine.solvers.cost_accounting.WorkloadLeverModel()
Cost per accepted task by workload, C_eff = C_attempt / p_acc, and three levers.
Halving the token price saves half the model share; halving the largest term saves half its share; raising acceptance by dp saves dp / (p + dp) of every term, and also removes the handoffs charged per rejected attempt. Acceptance beats halving tokens whenever the model share is below 2 dp / (p + dp).

title: engine.solvers.proposer
text:
engine.solvers.proposer
Learned-proposer solvers: what one fresh evaluation costs, and how long its evidence lasts.
Domain implementations behind mlsysim.solvers (the public import path, derived from engine.solvers.__init__). The equations live in physics.transformer (the roofline latency of one vision-language-action evaluation) and physics.robotics (chunk streaming, the renewal schedule, the tracked evidence horizon); these models compose them for one stated machine or situation (added 2026-10-20).





Name
Description




DecoderFamiliesModel
One fresh H-step chunk from a VLA backbone, for each decoder family.


EvidenceHorizonModel
How long a chunk’s evidence stays true for a tracked target, against its renewal schedule.


ProposerTrafficModel
Weight traffic of a machine’s two learned proposers on its shared memory bus.


VlaEvaluationModel
One fresh evaluation of a decoder-only VLA backbone on one processor.





engine.solvers.proposer.DecoderFamiliesModel()
One fresh H-step chunk from a VLA backbone, for each decoder family.
Every family pays the backbone’s prefill. Binned autoregressive decoding emits horizon * action_dim tokens one sweep at a time; FAST emits fast_tokens compressed tokens one at a time; a parallel head folds the binned tokens into one longer prefill; a flow-matching expert runs expert_steps refinement steps, each max(compute, (expert weights + cached prefix KV) / B_sustained) (Black et al. 2024; Pertsch et al. 2025; Kim, Finn and Liang 2025).



engine.solvers.proposer.EvidenceHorizonModel()
How long a chunk’s evidence stays true for a tracked target, against its renewal schedule.
Untracked, a target at speed v uses up the margin r_tol - e_0 in (r_tol - e_0) / v. Tracked, only a residual acceleration remains, so the evidence horizon is sqrt(2 (r_tol - e_0) / a_slip) (calc_tracked_evidence_horizon). The chunk policy’s renewal schedule (calc_chunk_renewal_schedule) gives the evidence age at replacement (renewal period plus inference), the setpoints one renewal needs, and the span one chunk supplies; drift over an age T is a_slip T^2 / 2.



engine.solvers.proposer.ProposerTrafficModel()
Weight traffic of a machine’s two learned proposers on its shared memory bus.
The intent model’s 16-bit sweep M / (B eta) bounds its fresh rate; spread over a chunk of H setpoints it is t / H per setpoint (calc_action_chunk_streaming_amortization). One sweep per setpoint at the setpoint rate would demand f_setpoint M; one per chunk divides that by H. In operation the deployed intent model sweeps its weights once per action token per evaluation (D M_deployed f_intent) and the chunk policy once per renewal (M_chunk f_chunk); their sum against the sustained bandwidth is the proposers’ share of the bus (weight traffic only).



engine.solvers.proposer.VlaEvaluationModel()
One fresh evaluation of a decoder-only VLA backbone on one processor.
Wraps calc_vla_inference_latency (compute-bound prefill, then action_tokens - 1 bandwidth-bound decode sweeps, or one longer prefill under parallel decoding) and adds the roofline coordinates of its two phases: the ridge R_peak / BW_peak at the 16-bit rate, the prefill intensity (linear FLOPs per weight byte, about S at 16-bit weights), and the decode intensity (2 N FLOP per weight sweep per weight byte, 1 at 16-bit weights).

title: engine.solvers.mapping
text:
engine.solvers.mapping
Volumetric-map solvers: clearance-query reads, map storage, update traffic, and encoder rate (added 2026-10-20).
Domain implementations behind mlsysim.solvers. The equations live in physics/robotics/perception.py; these models compose them for one stated permission controller, workcell, depth stream, or encoder.





Name
Description




ClearanceQueryModel
Reads a sphere-hull clearance query needs per map representation, against the permission tick’s read budget.


EncoderRateModel
A per-frame encoder of flop_per_frame run at frame_rate, against a peak rate.


HostMapSizingModel
A dense voxel grid of a workcell against a hashed narrow band around its surfaces.


RaymarchTrafficModel
Naive ray-marching map-update traffic f N_rays (d / r) S against a memory bandwidth.





engine.solvers.mapping.ClearanceQueryModel()
Reads a sphere-hull clearance query needs per map representation, against the permission tick’s read budget.
The collision allocation divided among the hulls gives the time per query; SRAM bandwidth over that time, in cells, is the read budget. An occupancy scan reads calc_sphere_scan_cells cells; an octree pays calc_octree_depth dependent reads for each; an ESDF reads the corners of one trilinear interpolation. A snapshot of slab_volume stores V / r^3 cells, and a cell’s center misplaces a point by up to calc_voxel_quantization_error.



engine.solvers.mapping.EncoderRateModel()
A per-frame encoder of flop_per_frame run at frame_rate, against a peak rate.



engine.solvers.mapping.HostMapSizingModel()
A dense voxel grid of a workcell against a hashed narrow band around its surfaces.
Dense storage is V / r^3 voxels; the band of half-width delta around surface area A has volume 2 delta A and fills V_band / (B r)^3 blocks of B^3 voxels each.



engine.solvers.mapping.RaymarchTrafficModel()
Naive ray-marching map-update traffic f N_rays (d / r) S against a memory bandwidth.

title: solvers.CheckpointModel
text:
solvers.CheckpointModel()
Analyzes the storage constraints and I/O burst penalties of saving model states.
Training massive models requires saving hundreds of gigabytes (Weights + Optimizer States) to persistent storage. This model calculates the time spent blocked on I/O, subtracting from the cluster’s Model FLOPs Utilization.
Literature Source: 1. Eisenman et al. (2022), “Check-N-Run: A Checkpointing System for Training Large Language Models.”





Name
Description




solve
Solves for checkpoint size, write time, and resulting MFU penalty.





solvers.CheckpointModel.solve(
    model,
    hardware,
    optimizer='adam',
    checkpoint_interval_hours=4.0,
    n_writers=1,
    filesystem_limit_gbs=500.0,
)
Solves for checkpoint size, write time, and resulting MFU penalty.











Name
Type
Description
Default




n_writers
int
Number of parallel checkpoint writers (default 1). Distributed checkpointing (e.g., FSDP) shards the write across workers.
1


filesystem_limit_gbs
float
Maximum aggregate filesystem write bandwidth in GB/s (default 500). Prevents over-optimistic scaling when n_writers is large.
500.0

title: physics.coordination
text:
physics.coordination
Coordination of several agents: partitions, schedules, shared writes, and correlated votes.
Added 2026-10-20. Each function is the arithmetic of one coordination relation: the elapsed time of a work partition with a per-worker overhead, the deliveries of a full mesh against a supervisor, the earliest schedule of a dependency graph, the chance that independent write sets stay disjoint, the binomial and beta-binomial tails of a vote, and the beta mass above a threshold that floors a correlated majority.





Name
Description




calc_beta_binomial_pmf
Beta-binomial masses for 0 to trials successes.


calc_beta_mixture_shape
Beta shape (a, b) with the given mean and pairwise (intraclass) correlation.


calc_beta_tail
Mass of the beta law (given mean and correlation) above threshold.


calc_binomial_tail
Probability of at least at_least successes in trials independent trials.


calc_disjoint_writes
Probability that N write sets of w files each, drawn uniformly from F, are pairwise disjoint.


calc_disjoint_writes_approx
The birthday approximation of :func:calc_disjoint_writes: exp(-N (N - 1) w^2 / (2 F)).


calc_earliest_schedule
Earliest start and finish of every node of an acyclic dependency graph with unlimited slots.


calc_full_mesh_deliveries
Directed deliveries when each of N participants sends to every other once: N (N - 1).


calc_partition_elapsed
Elapsed time of a fixed partition, as a fraction of the serial reference.


calc_supervisor_deliveries
Deliveries when a supervisor sends one envelope to and receives one receipt from each worker: 2 N.





physics.coordination.calc_beta_binomial_pmf(trials, mean, correlation)
Beta-binomial masses for 0 to trials successes.
Each trial succeeds with a propensity drawn once from a beta law of the given mean and pairwise correlation; the masses use log gamma functions.



physics.coordination.calc_beta_mixture_shape(mean, correlation)
Beta shape (a, b) with the given mean and pairwise (intraclass) correlation.
a = mean (1/rho - 1),  b = (1 - mean)(1/rho - 1)



physics.coordination.calc_beta_tail(mean, correlation, threshold)
Mass of the beta law (given mean and correlation) above threshold.
As a correlated panel grows, the share of members that err converges to the item’s propensity, so a majority errs on exactly the items whose propensity exceeds one half: this mass is the floor under majority error.



physics.coordination.calc_binomial_tail(trials, probability, at_least)
Probability of at least at_least successes in trials independent trials.



physics.coordination.calc_disjoint_writes(workers, files, writes_per_worker)
Probability that N write sets of w files each, drawn uniformly from F, are pairwise disjoint.
prod_{k=1}^{N-1} C(F - k w, w) / C(F, w)
Worker k + 1 must avoid the k w files already written.



physics.coordination.calc_disjoint_writes_approx(
    workers,
    files,
    writes_per_worker,
)
The birthday approximation of :func:calc_disjoint_writes: exp(-N (N - 1) w^2 / (2 F)).



physics.coordination.calc_earliest_schedule(durations, predecessors)
Earliest start and finish of every node of an acyclic dependency graph with unlimited slots.
durations maps each node to its time; predecessors maps it to the nodes that must finish first. A node starts when its last predecessor finishes. Returns (start, finish) dictionaries in the order of durations; the makespan is the latest finish, the critical path.



physics.coordination.calc_full_mesh_deliveries(workers)
Directed deliveries when each of N participants sends to every other once: N (N - 1).



physics.coordination.calc_partition_elapsed(
    workers,
    parallel_fraction,
    overhead_per_extra_worker,
)
Elapsed time of a fixed partition, as a fraction of the serial reference.
T(N) / T(1) = (1 - p) + p / N + c (N - 1)
p is the share of the work that divides among N workers and c the coordination overhead each added worker costs, both normalized by the serial time. With sigma = 1 - p and kappa = c this is the reciprocal of the universal scalability law’s capacity.



physics.coordination.calc_supervisor_deliveries(workers)
Deliveries when a supervisor sends one envelope to and receives one receipt from each worker: 2 N.

title: solvers.ResponsibleEngineeringModel
text:
solvers.ResponsibleEngineeringModel()
Models the computational cost of responsible AI practices (Wall 20: Safety).
This model quantifies the ‘Safety Tax’ — the additional compute and data required for differential privacy or fairness guarantees.
Literature Source: 1. Abadi et al. (2016), “Deep Learning with Differential Privacy.” 2. Anil et al. (2022), “Large-Scale Differentially Private BERT.”





Name
Description




solve
Calculate the compute and data overhead of responsible-AI guarantees.





solvers.ResponsibleEngineeringModel.solve(
    base_training_time,
    epsilon=1.0,
    delta=1e-05,
    min_subgroup_prevalence=0.01,
)
Calculate the compute and data overhead of responsible-AI guarantees.
Two first-order cost models:

Privacy (DP-SGD slowdown): slowdown = 1 + coefficient / epsilon — tighter privacy budgets (smaller epsilon) require more noise and per-sample clipping work, so training time grows hyperbolically as epsilon -> 0. The coefficient is a pedagogical calibration constant (DP_SGD_SLOWDOWN_COEFFICIENT in engine/calibration.py).
Fairness (data requirement): additional_data = 1 / min_subgroup_prevalence — to collect N samples of a subgroup seen at prevalence p, you must collect ~N/p samples overall.












Name
Type
Description
Default




base_training_time
Quantity
Training time without privacy guarantees (any time unit; the result keeps the same unit).
required


epsilon
float
Differential-privacy budget (> 0); smaller is stricter. Clamped below at 0.01 to avoid a singular slowdown.
1.0


delta
float
DP failure probability (reported, not used in the slowdown model).
1e-05


min_subgroup_prevalence
float
Prevalence in (0, 1] of the rarest subgroup that must be adequately represented.
0.01














Name
Type
Description





ResponsibleEngineeringResult
DP slowdown factor (dimensionless), effective training time, and the data-collection multiplier.

Memory footprint in bytes.







physics.robotics.perception.calc_free_space_expiry(
    free_depth,
    loc_bound,
    protective_clearance,
    approach_speed,
)
Calculate how long a free-space claim survives before an unseen person could breach the clearance.
Equation: T_inv = max(0, (d_free - delta_loc - delta_margin) / v_h)
The free region erodes from its unobserved boundary at the approach speed v_h; localization error delta_loc and the protective clearance delta_margin are spent up front. It is calc_linear_invalidation_horizon with E_0 = delta_loc, r = v_h, and E_max = d_free - delta_margin.
Source: linear invalidation horizon applied to occluded free space; the walking-speed bound v_h is ISO 13855’s K (1.6 m/s).



physics.robotics.perception.calc_linear_invalidation_horizon(
    initial_error,
    error_growth_rate,
    error_limit,
)
Calculate the invalidation horizon of a belief whose error bound grows linearly.
Equation: E(dt) = E_0 + r * dt ; T_inv = max(0, (E_max - E_0) / r)
A zero result means the belief never supported the task: its initial error already consumes the tolerance. Unlike calc_target_evidence_horizon this does not raise when E_0 >= E_max; it floors the deadline at zero.
Source: first-passage time of a linear error bound (definition of the invalidation horizon, T_inv = inf{dt >= 0 : E(dt) >= E_max}); the reachable-set lineage for occluded free space is Orzechowski, Meyer, and Lauer 2018 (IEEE ITSC).



physics.robotics.perception.calc_octree_depth(map_edge, pitch)
Levels an octree descends from a cube of edge map_edge to leaves of edge pitch.
Equation: depth = ceil(log2(L / r))
Each level is one dependent read in a point query.
Source: Hornung et al., “OctoMap,” Autonomous Robots 34(3), 2013, Sec. III.

Source: OpenStax, University Physics Volume 1, Sec. 3.1. Physical AI perception pipeline waterfall (exposure, readout, transport, DMA, ISP, backbone, IPC).

reach is the sphere radius plus the protective clearance; every cell within it must be read, because an occupancy cell answers only whether that one cell is occupied.

This is not a stopping-time or stopping-distance bound. Motion admission also needs current clearance, total pre-brake delay, achievable deceleration, and a feasible fallback after this evidence expires.

physics.robotics.perception.calc_tracked_evidence_horizon(
    tolerance_radius,
    initial_error,
    slip_acceleration,
)
Calculate the tracked target-evidence horizon under residual slip acceleration.
A tracker that follows a moving target removes its steady velocity, so the remaining error growth comes from a bounded residual acceleration a_slip. A segment executed open-loop for a time T then drifts by a_slip T^2 / 2; setting that drift equal to the error margin r_tol - e_0 gives
Equation: tau_ev = sqrt(2 (r_tol - e_0) / a_slip)
This is the constant-acceleration counterpart of calc_target_evidence_horizon (constant drift velocity, a_slip = 0). Like that function it is not a stopping-time bound.
Source: first-passage time of a constant-acceleration displacement (d = a T^2 / 2, solved for T at d = r_tol - e_0); kinematics, derived here.

required

required

required

physics.robotics.perception.calc_tsdf_voxel_grid_budget(
    workspace_volume,
    voxel_size,
    bytes_per_voxel=4,
    sparsity_ratio=0.03,
    block_size_voxels=512,
    block_header_bytes=32,
    ray_rate=None,
    dense_voxels_per_ray=300,
    sparse_voxels_per_ray=6,
    free_voxels_per_ray=294,
    bytes_per_ray_voxel=8,
    cache_hit_rate=0.95,
)
Calculate partial TSDF storage and modeled DRAM traffic for dense vs sparse grids.
The four-byte voxel stores distance and fusion weight only. The sparse result includes the stipulated leaf header, but neither result includes a separate occupancy layer, per-cell evidence epochs, lookup/allocator metadata, or other full-map state. The hit rate is an assumed workload input, not a property of sparse allocation.
Equation: N_dense = V_workspace / (Delta_v)^3 M_dense = N_dense * B_voxel N_active = N_dense * S_sparsity N_blocks = ceil(N_active / B_block) M_sparse = N_blocks * (B_block * B_voxel + B_header) BW_dense_dram = R_rays * N_dense_lookups * B_lookup BW_sparse_dram = R_rays * (N_free_occupancy + N_TSDF_band) * B_lookup * (1 - Hit_cache)











Name
Type
Description
Default




workspace_volume
Quantity
Total bounding volume of operational workcell (e.g. 300 m^3).
required


voxel_size
Quantity
Isotropic voxel side length (e.g. 1.0 cm or 5.0 mm).
required


bytes_per_voxel
int
TSDF payload bytes per voxel (default 4: 16-bit distance + 16-bit weight).
4


sparsity_ratio
float
Surface occupancy fraction within bounding volume (default 0.03 = 3%).
0.03


block_size_voxels
int
Voxel count per hierarchical leaf block (default 512 for 8x8x8).
512


block_header_bytes
int
Memory overhead per block metadata/pointer header (default 32 B).
32


ray_rate
Quantity
Raycast integration query rate (e.g., 640x480x60 = 18.432e6 rays/s).
None


dense_voxels_per_ray
int
Raycast integration depth across dense volume (default 300 lookups).
300


sparse_voxels_per_ray
int
TSDF fusion updates in the narrow surface band (default 6 lookups).
6


free_voxels_per_ray
int
Separate occupancy free-ray updates before the hit (default 294). Sparse TSDF allocation does not remove this traversal or its occupancy work.
294


bytes_per_ray_voxel
int
Read-modify-write memory traffic per ray step (default 8 B).
8


cache_hit_rate
float
Assumed measured SRAM/L2 hit fraction for both occupancy and TSDF updates (default 0.95 for the illustrative scenario; not a sparse-map property).
0.95

Type
Description





dict

Calculate the tracked target-evidence horizon under residual slip acceleration.
A tracker that follows a moving target removes its steady velocity, so the remaining error growth comes from a bounded residual acceleration a_slip. A segment executed open-loop for a time T then drifts by a_slip T^2 / 2; setting that drift equal to the error margin r_tol - e_0 gives

title: solvers.SustainabilityModel
text:
solvers.SustainabilityModel()
Calculates Datacenter-scale Sustainability metrics.
Handles Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE), Carbon Intensity, and Water Usage Effectiveness (WUE) across different regional grids. This model simulates the ‘Infrastructure Tax’ — the energy spent on cooling and power delivery rather than on neural computation.
Literature Source: 1. Patterson et al. (2021), “Carbon Emissions and Large Neural Network Training.” 2. Belkhir & Elmeligi (2018), “Assessing ICT Global Emissions Footprint.” 3. Wu et al. (2022), “Sustainable AI: Environmental Implications, Challenges and Opportunities.”
Formula contract: - per-device power = idle_fraction * TDP + dynamic_fraction * TDP * MFU. - IT energy = device power * accelerator count * duration. - facility energy applies PUE; operational carbon applies grid carbon intensity to facility energy; water applies WUE to facility energy.





Name
Description




solve
Calculate energy, carbon, and water footprint for a fleet operation.





solvers.SustainabilityModel.solve(
    fleet,
    duration_days,
    datacenter=None,
    mfu=1.0,
    embodied_carbon_per_device=0.0,
)
Calculate energy, carbon, and water footprint for a fleet operation.
Implements the formula contract in the class docstring: per-device power is an energy-proportionality model (idle_fraction * TDP + dynamic_fraction * TDP * MFU), scaled to the fleet, integrated over the duration, then taxed by PUE for facility energy. Carbon and water apply the regional grid’s carbon intensity and WUE to facility (post-PUE) energy.

title: solvers.OrchestrationModel
text:
solvers.OrchestrationModel()
Analyzes Cluster Orchestration and Queueing (Little’s Law).
Caveat: This model uses a pedagogical M/D/1 queue (single server, deterministic service) to establish macroscopic wait-time bounds for dedicated, monolithic cluster workloads. For detailed multi-tenant job packing and preemption, a discrete-event M/G/c scheduler simulation would be required.
This model simulates the ‘Wait Wall’ in shared research clusters, calculating job completion times and researcher wait times based on cluster utilization and arrival rates.
Literature Source: 1. Little (1961), “A Proof for the Queuing Formula: L = λW.” 2. Barroso et al. (2018), “The Datacenter as a Computer” (Cluster Mgmt). 3. Jeon et al. (2019), “Analysis of Large-Scale Multi-Tenant GPU Clusters.”

physics.reliability.calc_all_up_availability(availability, n_components)
Probability that all of N independent components are up at once: a**N.
A synchronous job that needs every one of N components is available only when all are; with independent failures that is the product of the per-component availabilities. Added 2026-10-20.



physics.reliability.calc_availability_stacked(single_availability, n_replicas)
System availability with k independent replicas.



physics.reliability.calc_checkpoint_stride(pause, crash_rate, lost_turn_cost)
Checkpoint stride, in turns, that balances pauses against work lost to crashes.
Young’s (1974) balance counted in turns: a checkpoint every k turns costs pause / k per turn, and a crash (crash_rate per turn) loses k / 2 turns on average, each costing lost_turn_cost to recover. The per-turn overhead pause / k + crash_rate * lost_turn_cost * k / 2 is least at k* = sqrt(2 pause / (crash_rate * lost_turn_cost)).



physics.reliability.calc_checkpoint_waste(write_time, interval, mtbf)
First-order share of wall time lost to checkpointing at interval.
W = write_time / interval + interval / (2 * mtbf): each save pauses training for write_time once per interval, and each failure (one per mtbf) discards half an interval of work on average (Young 1974). At the Young-Daly interval the two terms are equal and W = sqrt(2 * write_time / mtbf). Added 2026-10-20.



physics.reliability.calc_downtime(availability, interval)
Expected time down in interval at a steady-state availability.



physics.reliability.calc_error_budget_spent(burn_rate, window, budget_period)
Share of an SLO’s error budget spent by a sustained burn rate (added 2026-10-20).
A burn rate of 1 spends exactly the budget over budget_period; a burn rate b sustained for window spends b * window / budget_period (Google SRE Workbook, “Alerting on SLOs”).



physics.reliability.calc_failure_probability(mtbf, job_duration)
Probability of at least one failure during a job.
Poisson/exponential failure model: P = 1 - exp(-T / MTBF). For short jobs (T << MTBF) this approaches T / MTBF; as T grows it saturates at 1.

Type
Description
Default




mtbf
Quantity or float
Mean time between failures (> 0).
required


job_duration
Quantity or float
Job length. Both arguments must be Quantities (any time units) or both raw numbers in the same unit — mixing raises TypeError because the implied unit would be ambiguous.
required

Type

Dimensionless probability in [0, 1).







physics.reliability.calc_group_commit_waits(batch_timer, flush_time, batch_size)
Storage work per record and the waits of the first and last arrivals in one group commit.
One flush of flush_time acknowledges batch_size queued records (DeWitt et al. 1984). The work charged to each record is flush_time / batch_size, but every record waits for the whole flush: the first arrival also waits out the batch_timer that gathers the batch, the last waits the flush alone. Returns (work_per_record, first_wait, last_wait).



physics.reliability.calc_mtbf_cluster(
    component_mtbf_hours,
    n_components,
    correlation_factor=1.0,
)
Cluster MTBF from identical independent components.
MTBF_cluster = MTBF_component / N — exact when failures are independent and exponentially distributed (the minimum of N i.i.d. exponentials is exponential with N times the rate).
correlation_factor scales the result: values below 1 model correlated/clustered failures making the effective cluster MTBF worse (0.5 halves it); 1.0 (default) is the independent case.



physics.reliability.calc_mtbf_node(
    gpu_mtbf_h,
    n_gpus,
    nic_mtbf_h,
    n_nics,
    psu_mtbf_h,
    n_psus,
    other_mtbf_h=None,
    n_other=0,
)
Compound node MTBF from heterogeneous components (series system).
Assumes independent, exponentially distributed failures where any single component failure fails the node, so failure rates add: MTBF_node = 1 / (n_gpu/MTBF_gpu + n_nic/MTBF_nic + n_psu/MTBF_psu + ...). Redundant PSUs (N+M, M >= 1) do not fail the node singly; pass Node.series_psus (0 for a redundant supply) rather than the physical PSU count.

physics.reliability.calc_probe_detection_window(
    interval,
    timeout,
    failure_threshold,
)
Earliest and latest time from a crash to removal by a health probe.
A replica leaves rotation after failure_threshold consecutive failed probes, each failing timeout after it starts. A crash just before a probe is removed after (threshold - 1) * interval + timeout; a crash just after a successful probe waits one more interval. Added 2026-10-20.



physics.reliability.calc_snapshot_write_volume(
    state_growth,
    stride,
    checkpoints,
)
Bytes written by full snapshots and by deltas over checkpoints checkpoints.
State grows by state_growth per turn and a checkpoint is taken every stride turns. Checkpoint m of a full-snapshot policy rewrites all m * stride * state_growth accumulated so far, so the total is state_growth * stride * n (n + 1) / 2; deltas write each turn’s growth once, state_growth * stride * n. Returns (full, delta).



physics.reliability.calc_step_event_probability(
    rate_per_device_hour,
    n_devices,
    step_time,
)
Probability that at least one of n_devices meets an event during one step.
Each device meets events at rate_per_device_hour (a probability per device-hour); one step exposes n_devices * step_time device-hours, so p = 1 - (1 - rate) ** exposure. Used for silent-data-corruption exposure across a synchronous job. Added 2026-10-20.



physics.reliability.calc_stride_overhead(
    pause,
    stride,
    crash_rate,
    lost_turn_cost,
)
Expected overhead per turn at checkpoint stride: pause / k + rate * cost * k / 2 (seconds).



physics.reliability.calc_young_daly_interval(checkpoint_cost_s, mtbf_s)
Optimal checkpoint interval: tau = sqrt(2 * delta * MTBF).
Young (1974) first-order approximation, popularized with the Daly (2006) refinement; this implements the Young form, which balances time lost to checkpointing against expected rework after a failure. Valid when delta << MTBF (the usual regime; otherwise use Daly’s higher-order form).

required

Redundant PSUs (N+M, M >= 1) do not fail the node singly; pass Node.series_psus (0 for a redundant supply) rather than the physical PSU count.

physics.reliability.calc_probe_detection_window(
    interval,
    timeout,
    failure_threshold,
)
Earliest and latest time from a crash to removal by a health probe.
A replica leaves rotation after failure_threshold consecutive failed probes, each failing timeout after it starts. A crash just before a probe is removed after (threshold - 1) * interval + timeout; a crash just after a successful probe waits one more interval. Added 2026-10-20.



physics.reliability.calc_snapshot_write_volume(
    state_growth,
    stride,
    checkpoints,
)
Bytes written by full snapshots and by deltas over checkpoints checkpoints.
State grows by state_growth per turn and a checkpoint is taken every stride turns. Checkpoint m of a full-snapshot policy rewrites all m * stride * state_growth accumulated so far, so the total is state_growth * stride * n (n + 1) / 2; deltas write each turn’s growth once, state_growth * stride * n. Returns (full, delta).



physics.reliability.calc_step_event_probability(
    rate_per_device_hour,
    n_devices,
    step_time,
)
Probability that at least one of n_devices meets an event during one step.
Each device meets events at rate_per_device_hour (a probability per device-hour); one step exposes n_devices * step_time device-hours, so p = 1 - (1 - rate) ** exposure. Used for silent-data-corruption exposure across a synchronous job. Added 2026-10-20.



physics.reliability.calc_stride_overhead(
    pause,
    stride,
    crash_rate,
    lost_turn_cost,
)
Expected overhead per turn at checkpoint stride: pause / k + rate * cost * k / 2 (seconds).



physics.reliability.calc_young_daly_interval(checkpoint_cost_s, mtbf_s)
Optimal checkpoint interval: tau = sqrt(2 * delta * MTBF).
Young (1974) first-order approximation, popularized with the Daly (2006) refinement; this implements the Young form, which balances time lost to checkpointing against expected rework after a failure. Valid when delta << MTBF (the usual regime; otherwise use Daly’s higher-order form).

fmt.fmt
fmt.fmt(
    quantity,

    precision=1,
    commas=True,
    prefix='',
    suffix='',
    approx=False,
    lower_bound=False,

)
Format a Pint Quantity (or plain number) for narrative text. Returns a MarkdownStr so Quarto inserts the value verbatim (no escape).
The prefix and suffix arguments collapse the old MarkdownStr(f”…“) escape-hatch idiom into a single canonical helper. Common uses:
fmt(value, precision=0, approx=True)       # "~1,000"
fmt(value, precision=0, lower_bound=True)  # "> 1,000"
fmt_percent(rate, precision=1, style="symbol")  # "12.4%"
fmt_qty(bandwidth, unit=MB/second)         # "2.4 MB/s"
fmt_multiple(speedup)                      # "3.2×"
Safety: Raises ValueError if formatting would hide meaningful magnitude: non-zero values displayed as 0, non-integers displayed with precision=0, or integer-like values shown with spurious decimals (512.0). Use fmt_int(...) when integer display is intentional.

solvers.StereoDepthErrorModel
solvers.StereoDepthErrorModel()
One-sigma stereo depth error against range, and where it spends each clearance.
sigma_z = z^2 sigma_d / (f b) grows with squared range; the range at which one sigma equals a clearance C is sqrt(C f b / sigma_d). Adding one sigma to a clearance kept along the viewing ray is the shortcut inset; an unmodeled baseline change db biases depth by z db / b.

title: solvers.WeightStreamingModel
text:
solvers.WeightStreamingModel()
Analyzes Wafer-Scale inference (e.g., Cerebras CS-3) using Weight Streaming.
Instead of holding weights in HBM and streaming activations (the GPU Memory Wall), this architecture holds massive activation batches on-wafer (SRAM) and streams the model weights from external MemoryX nodes.
The bottleneck shifts from Memory Bandwidth to Injection Interconnect Bandwidth.

title: engine.solvers.operations
text:
engine.solvers.operations
Agent-operations solvers: traces, retention, and staged release (added 2026-10-20).
Domain implementations behind mlsysim.solvers. Each model is arithmetic on stated inputs: the elapsed time one trial’s spans explain along its critical path, and what shortening one span saves; the diagnostic trace bodies head sampling and verdict-aware selection keep; and a Wald sequential test run as a canary monitor, in labeled tasks, calendar time, and excess failures. None models a particular tracing system, collector, or rollout controller.





Name
Description




SequentialCanaryModel
A Wald SPRT on task acceptance run as a canary monitor.


SpanCriticalPathModel
One trial’s spans on a shared clock: what they explain, and what one shorter span saves.


TraceRetentionModel
Diagnostic trace bodies kept over a window under three selections.





engine.solvers.operations.SequentialCanaryModel()
A Wald SPRT on task acceptance run as a canary monitor.
The log-likelihood ratio favors the degraded acceptance p_degraded over p_base: a failure adds ln((1 - p1)/(1 - p0)) and a success ln(p1/p0) (the negated increments of calc_sprt_increments on the failure probabilities). Wald’s boundaries come from the false-hold target alpha and the missed-degradation target beta (calc_sprt_boundaries). Under the degraded hypothesis the walk ends at the upper boundary with probability 1 - beta; neglecting overshoot, calc_sprt_expected_samples gives the expected labeled tasks. Labels arrive label_delay after admission at fraction of the eligible arrival_rate, so calendar time scales as 1/fraction while the measured regression’s excess failures change only through the tasks admitted while labels are pending.



engine.solvers.operations.SpanCriticalPathModel()
One trial’s spans on a shared clock: what they explain, and what one shorter span saves.
Each span has an observed interval and the spans it waits for. Summing every span counts overlapping work twice; the critical path (calc_cleanup_critical_path) counts the longest dependent chain once. The elapsed segment less that path is time no span explains. For an intervention, every span keeps its observed wait after its predecessors (the unexplained gap stays where it was) and takes its new duration.



engine.solvers.operations.TraceRetentionModel()
Diagnostic trace bodies kept over a window under three selections.
Keeping every body stores the whole cohort. Head sampling keeps each trial with one probability, decided before its outcome, so it keeps that share of the failures too. Verdict-aware (tail) selection keeps every failed and unresolved trial and a random control share of the ordinary ones; its volume is a floor set by the failure-plus-unresolved rate plus a term linear in the control share. Classes are disjoint and every body has the same size.

physics.agents
Agentic ML systems physics and memory accounting formulas (Volume III).

Description

physics.agents.calc_append_only_context(initial_tokens, tokens_per_turn, turns)
Context of the last call and total input sent by an append-only trajectory.
Turn t (from 1) reads s0 + delta (t - 1) tokens, so the last of H turns reads s0 + delta (H - 1), and the H calls together send
H s0 + delta H (H - 1) / 2
tokens: input grows quadratically with the horizon when every turn resends the history. Returns (last_call, cumulative).



physics.agents.calc_bounded_liability(
    input_tokens,
    output_allowance,
    input_price,
    output_price,
)
Most one model call can bill before it settles.
L = n_in p_in + K_out p_out
Every input token is priced at the undiscounted input rate (a cache hit is not guaranteed before dispatch) and the whole output allowance at the output rate. Prices are per token, in any one currency unit.



physics.agents.calc_break_even_acceptance(acceptance_probability, cut, share)
Acceptance that matches a price cut on one component of the attempt cost.
Removing a fraction cut of a component that is share of the attempt cost gives the same cost per accepted task as raising acceptance to
p' = p_acc / (1 - cut * share)



physics.agents.calc_cleanup_critical_path(durations, depends_on)
Elapsed time of a cleanup graph run with unlimited parallelism.
durations maps each operation to its time once admitted; depends_on maps it to the operations that must settle first. The elapsed time is the longest path through the acyclic graph; a reverse stack runs the same operations one at a time and takes their sum.



physics.agents.calc_cost_per_accepted(attempt_cost, acceptance_probability)
Expected cost per accepted task when attempts repeat until one is accepted.
C_eff = E[C_attempt] / p_acc
Attempts are geometric with mean 1 / p_acc, so every rejected attempt is charged to the accepted one.



physics.agents.calc_cost_per_rejection(check_cost, pass_probability)
Checking cost spent per record a check rejects: t / (1 - p).
For two adjacent independent checks, running A first is cheaper when A’s cost per rejection is lower (the rank ordering of expensive predicates).



physics.agents.calc_drr_calls_per_round(weight, quantum, charge)
Long-run calls per round of a backlogged class under weighted deficit round-robin.
calls/round = w q / c
The class earns w q charge units of credit per round and spends c per call; unspent credit carries over, so the rate holds on average even when one call needs several rounds of credit (Shreedhar and Varghese 1995).



physics.agents.calc_expected_irreversible_loss(
    defect_probability,
    consequence,
    recoverable_fraction,
)
Expected loss that no recovery action can undo.
L = P(defect) x consequence x (1 - r)
r is the fraction of a defect’s consequence that recovery avoids; a check ahead of the pivot that catches a fraction v and reverts with fidelity rho gives r = v rho.



physics.agents.calc_expected_max_std_normal(n, lo=-10.0, hi=10.0, steps=40000)
Expected maximum of n independent standard normals (trapezoidal integral).
E[max] = integral of x * n * phi(x) * Phi(x)^(n - 1) dx
The winner of an argmax over n equally good candidates carries this much scoring error, in units of the score noise’s standard deviation.



physics.agents.calc_first_horizon_below(step_success, threshold)
First whole horizon n at which step_success ** n falls below threshold.
n = floor(ln(threshold) / ln(step_success)) + 1



physics.agents.calc_independent_success(acceptance_probability, attempts)
Chance that at least one of attempts independent attempts is accepted.
1 - (1 - p_acc)^k



physics.agents.calc_injection_exposure(payload_fraction, reads)
Chance that a task reading reads independent untrusted items meets a payload.
Pr(exp) = 1 - (1 - q)^n
q is the fraction of items carrying a payload. While q n is small, Pr(exp) ~ q n; a screen that misses a fraction m of payloads replaces q with q m. Counted in turns, q is the per-turn chance and n the horizon.



physics.agents.calc_injection_read_budget(payload_fraction, target_exposure)
Most untrusted reads a task may make and keep exposure at or below target_exposure.
n_max = floor(ln(1 - target) / ln(1 - q))



physics.agents.calc_kv_cache_bytes_per_token(
    model=None,
    *,
    n_layers=None,
    n_kv_heads=None,
    head_dim=None,
    bytes_per_elem=2,
)
Calculate the Key-Value (KV) cache memory footprint per token.
For a transformer architecture with L layers, H_kv Key/Value attention heads, and head dimension d_head:
m_token = 2 * L * H_kv * d_head * bytes_per_elem
The leading factor of 2 accounts for storing separate Key and Value tensors.

Type
Description
Default




model
TransformerWorkload or AgentArchitecture
Model from which layers, heads, and dimensions are extracted.
None


n_layers
int
Number of transformer layers (if model is omitted).
None


n_kv_heads
int
Number of Key/Value attention heads (if model is omitted).
None


head_dim
int
Dimension per attention head (if model is omitted).
None


bytes_per_elem
Quantity or int
Numerical precision in bytes (default: 2 for FP16/BF16).
2









Name
Type
Description





Quantity
Memory size per token (in bytes).







physics.agents.calc_mixed_outcome_fraction(pass_probability, attempts)
Chance that attempts independent attempts hold at least one success and one failure.
1 - (1 - p)^k - p^k



physics.agents.calc_nucleus(probabilities, top_p)
Top-p truncation: the shortest highest-probability prefix whose mass reaches top_p.
Returns (kept, mass, renormalized): how many tokens stay, their total probability, and their probabilities rescaled to sum to one.



physics.agents.calc_pass_at_k_unbiased(samples, passing, k)
Unbiased pass@k from samples draws of which passing pass (Chen et al. 2021).
pass@k = 1 - C(n - c, k) / C(n, k)
the share of all size-k subsets that hold at least one pass; 1 when n - c < k.



physics.agents.calc_pass_posterior(
    defect_rate,
    false_accept_rate,
    valid_accept_rate,
)
Bayes’ rule: share of passing candidates that are defective, P(Def | PASS).



physics.agents.calc_pass_pow_k_unbiased(samples, passing, k)
Unbiased pass^k from samples graded runs of one task of which passing pass (Yao et al. 2024).
pass^k = C(c, k) / C(n, k)
the share of all size-k subsets in which every run passes; 0 when c < k. Its expectation is p^k, the mirror of the pass@k estimate calc_pass_at_k_unbiased (added 2026-10-20).



physics.agents.calc_pruned_tree_nodes(branching, rejection_rate, depth)
Nodes a search generates through depth levels, unpruned and with a step check.
Every retained node proposes b children; the check rejects each child independently with probability r, so b_eff = b (1 - r) children survive per node. Level d generates b^d nodes unpruned and b * b_eff^(d - 1) pruned. Returns (unpruned, pruned).



physics.agents.calc_repair_break_even(repair_cost, fallback_cost)
Success probability above which one repair attempt beats the fallback.
p* = C_repair / C_fallback
Holds when a failed attempt leaves the fallback available at unchanged cost; evaluate it separately for each resource axis (seconds, dollars).



physics.agents.calc_repair_first_expected_cost(
    repair_cost,
    fallback_cost,
    success_probability,
)
Expected cost of attempting repair first: C_repair + (1 - p) C_fallback.



physics.agents.calc_reused_prefix_prompt_tokens(turns, first_prompt, appended)
Fresh prefill over turns calls when each earlier prompt prefix is reused: S0 + (H - 1) D.



physics.agents.calc_setup_share(setup, work)
Share of a fresh call spent on setup: T_setup / (T_setup + W).



physics.agents.calc_short_circuit_cost(pass_probabilities, check_costs)
Expected checking cost and pass-through share of checks run in order, stopping at the first failure.
Check i runs only when every earlier check passed, so the expected cost is sum_i t_i prod_{j<i} p_j and the share that passes them all is prod_i p_i. Returns (expected_cost, passing_share).



physics.agents.calc_split_straddle(train_fraction, attempts)
Chance that a task’s attempts land on both sides of a random split of runs.
Each run goes to training independently with probability f; the task stays on one side only if every run goes the same way:
1 - f^k - (1 - f)^k



physics.agents.calc_step_error_for_target(target_success, horizon)
Per-step error rate that holds target_success over horizon unchecked steps.
eps = 1 - target^(1/H)
For small eps, eps * H ~ -ln(target) at any horizon.



physics.agents.calc_tempered_softmax(logits, temperature=1.0)
Softmax of logits / T: the sampling distribution at temperature T.



physics.agents.calc_unchecked_success(step_success, horizon)
Success of a task whose horizon steps must all be right, unchecked.
Pr(success) = (1 - eps)^H = p_step^H
Assumes independent steps, no check between them, and no recovery.



physics.agents.calc_used_fraction(used, allowance)
Share of one budget dimension consumed: rho = used / allowance.



physics.agents.calc_work_for_setup_cap(setup, cap)
Useful work per call that holds setup to a share phi: W >= T_setup (1 - phi) / phi.

Turn t (from 1) reads s0 + delta (t - 1) tokens, so the last of H turns reads s0 + delta (H - 1), and the H calls together send
H s0 + delta H (H - 1) / 2
tokens: input grows quadratically with the horizon when every turn resends the history. Returns (last_call, cumulative).



physics.agents.calc_bounded_liability(
    input_tokens,
    output_allowance,
    input_price,
    output_price,
)
Most one model call can bill before it settles.
L = n_in p_in + K_out p_out
Every input token is priced at the undiscounted input rate (a cache hit is not guaranteed before dispatch) and the whole output allowance at the output rate. Prices are per token, in any one currency unit.



physics.agents.calc_break_even_acceptance(acceptance_probability, cut, share)
Acceptance that matches a price cut on one component of the attempt cost.
Removing a fraction cut of a component that is share of the attempt cost gives the same cost per accepted task as raising acceptance to
p' = p_acc / (1 - cut * share)



physics.agents.calc_cleanup_critical_path(durations, depends_on)
Elapsed time of a cleanup graph run with unlimited parallelism.
durations maps each operation to its time once admitted; depends_on maps it to the operations that must settle first. The elapsed time is the longest path through the acyclic graph; a reverse stack runs the same operations one at a time and takes their sum.



physics.agents.calc_cost_per_accepted(attempt_cost, acceptance_probability)
Expected cost per accepted task when attempts repeat until one is accepted.
C_eff = E[C_attempt] / p_acc
Attempts are geometric with mean 1 / p_acc, so every rejected attempt is charged to the accepted one.



physics.agents.calc_cost_per_rejection(check_cost, pass_probability)
Checking cost spent per record a check rejects: t / (1 - p).
For two adjacent independent checks, running A first is cheaper when A’s cost per rejection is lower (the rank ordering of expensive predicates).



physics.agents.calc_drr_calls_per_round(weight, quantum, charge)
Long-run calls per round of a backlogged class under weighted deficit round-robin.
calls/round = w q / c
The class earns w q charge units of credit per round and spends c per call; unspent credit carries over, so the rate holds on average even when one call needs several rounds of credit (Shreedhar and Varghese 1995).



physics.agents.calc_expected_irreversible_loss(
    defect_probability,
    consequence,
    recoverable_fraction,
)
Expected loss that no recovery action can undo.
L = P(defect) x consequence x (1 - r)
r is the fraction of a defect’s consequence that recovery avoids; a check ahead of the pivot that catches a fraction v and reverts with fidelity rho gives r = v rho.



physics.agents.calc_expected_max_std_normal(n, lo=-10.0, hi=10.0, steps=40000)
Expected maximum of n independent standard normals (trapezoidal integral).
E[max] = integral of x * n * phi(x) * Phi(x)^(n - 1) dx
The winner of an argmax over n equally good candidates carries this much scoring error, in units of the score noise’s standard deviation.



physics.agents.calc_first_horizon_below(step_success, threshold)
First whole horizon n at which step_success ** n falls below threshold.
n = floor(ln(threshold) / ln(step_success)) + 1



physics.agents.calc_independent_success(acceptance_probability, attempts)
Chance that at least one of attempts independent attempts is accepted.
1 - (1 - p_acc)^k



physics.agents.calc_injection_exposure(payload_fraction, reads)
Chance that a task reading reads independent untrusted items meets a payload.
Pr(exp) = 1 - (1 - q)^n
q is the fraction of items carrying a payload. While q n is small, Pr(exp) ~ q n; a screen that misses a fraction m of payloads replaces q with q m. Counted in turns, q is the per-turn chance and n the horizon.



physics.agents.calc_injection_read_budget(payload_fraction, target_exposure)
Most untrusted reads a task may make and keep exposure at or below target_exposure.
n_max = floor(ln(1 - target) / ln(1 - q))



physics.agents.calc_kv_cache_bytes_per_token(
    model=None,
    *,
    n_layers=None,
    n_kv_heads=None,
    head_dim=None,
    bytes_per_elem=2,
)
Calculate the Key-Value (KV) cache memory footprint per token.
For a transformer architecture with L layers, H_kv Key/Value attention heads, and head dimension d_head:
m_token = 2 * L * H_kv * d_head * bytes_per_elem
The leading factor of 2 accounts for storing separate Key and Value tensors.

Type
Description
Default




model
TransformerWorkload or AgentArchitecture
Model from which layers, heads, and dimensions are extracted.
None


n_layers
int
Number of transformer layers (if model is omitted).
None


n_kv_heads
int
Number of Key/Value attention heads (if model is omitted).
None


head_dim
int
Dimension per attention head (if model is omitted).
None


bytes_per_elem
Quantity or int
Numerical precision in bytes (default: 2 for FP16/BF16).
2









Name
Type
Description





Quantity
Memory size per token (in bytes).







physics.agents.calc_mixed_outcome_fraction(pass_probability, attempts)
Chance that attempts independent attempts hold at least one success and one failure.
1 - (1 - p)^k - p^k



physics.agents.calc_nucleus(probabilities, top_p)
Top-p truncation: the shortest highest-probability prefix whose mass reaches top_p.
Returns (kept, mass, renormalized): how many tokens stay, their total probability, and their probabilities rescaled to sum to one.



physics.agents.calc_pass_at_k_unbiased(samples, passing, k)
Unbiased pass@k from samples draws of which passing pass (Chen et al. 2021).
pass@k = 1 - C(n - c, k) / C(n, k)
the share of all size-k subsets that hold at least one pass; 1 when n - c < k.



physics.agents.calc_pass_posterior(
    defect_rate,
    false_accept_rate,
    valid_accept_rate,
)
Bayes’ rule: share of passing candidates that are defective, P(Def | PASS).



physics.agents.calc_pass_pow_k_unbiased(samples, passing, k)
Unbiased pass^k from samples graded runs of one task of which passing pass (Yao et al. 2024).
pass^k = C(c, k) / C(n, k)
the share of all size-k subsets in which every run passes; 0 when c < k. Its expectation is p^k, the mirror of the pass@k estimate calc_pass_at_k_unbiased (added 2026-10-20).



physics.agents.calc_pruned_tree_nodes(branching, rejection_rate, depth)
Nodes a search generates through depth levels, unpruned and with a step check.
Every retained node proposes b children; the check rejects each child independently with probability r, so b_eff = b (1 - r) children survive per node. Level d generates b^d nodes unpruned and b * b_eff^(d - 1) pruned. Returns (unpruned, pruned).



physics.agents.calc_repair_break_even(repair_cost, fallback_cost)
Success probability above which one repair attempt beats the fallback.
p* = C_repair / C_fallback
Holds when a failed attempt leaves the fallback available at unchanged cost; evaluate it separately for each resource axis (seconds, dollars).



physics.agents.calc_repair_first_expected_cost(
    repair_cost,
    fallback_cost,
    success_probability,
)
Expected cost of attempting repair first: C_repair + (1 - p) C_fallback.



physics.agents.calc_reused_prefix_prompt_tokens(turns, first_prompt, appended)
Fresh prefill over turns calls when each earlier prompt prefix is reused: S0 + (H - 1) D.



physics.agents.calc_setup_share(setup, work)
Share of a fresh call spent on setup: T_setup / (T_setup + W).



physics.agents.calc_short_circuit_cost(pass_probabilities, check_costs)
Expected checking cost and pass-through share of checks run in order, stopping at the first failure.
Check i runs only when every earlier check passed, so the expected cost is sum_i t_i prod_{j<i} p_j and the share that passes them all is prod_i p_i. Returns (expected_cost, passing_share).



physics.agents.calc_split_straddle(train_fraction, attempts)
Chance that a task’s attempts land on both sides of a random split of runs.
Each run goes to training independently with probability f; the task stays on one side only if every run goes the same way:
1 - f^k - (1 - f)^k



physics.agents.calc_step_error_for_target(target_success, horizon)
Per-step error rate that holds target_success over horizon unchecked steps.
eps = 1 - target^(1/H)
For small eps, eps * H ~ -ln(target) at any horizon.



physics.agents.calc_tempered_softmax(logits, temperature=1.0)
Softmax of logits / T: the sampling distribution at temperature T.



physics.agents.calc_unchecked_success(step_success, horizon)
Success of a task whose horizon steps must all be right, unchecked.
Pr(success) = (1 - eps)^H = p_step^H
Assumes independent steps, no check between them, and no recovery.



physics.agents.calc_used_fraction(used, allowance)
Share of one budget dimension consumed: rho = used / allowance.



physics.agents.calc_work_for_setup_cap(setup, cap)
Useful work per call that holds setup to a share phi: W >= T_setup (1 - phi) / phi.

title: solvers.ContinuousBatchingModel
text:
solvers.ContinuousBatchingModel()
Compares static KV reservation with PagedAttention under continuous batching.
Decode is memory-bound, so the number of requests sharing a step is the throughput lever, and the KV-cache allocator decides how many fit. A static allocator reserves a contiguous slot of max_seq_len tokens for every request; PagedAttention hands out fixed-size blocks on demand. This model sizes both from the same KV budget and a request-length distribution, then compares memory-bound decode throughput at each allocator’s concurrency.
Kwon et al. (2023) profile contiguous pre-allocation (their Orca baselines) and find that only 20.4% to 38.2% of KV-cache memory holds actual token states (Fig. 2). The rest is reserved slots for future tokens, internal fragmentation from over-provisioning for the maximum sequence length, and external fragmentation from the memory allocator (Sec. 3.1, Fig. 3). vLLM limits each request’s waste to one block (Sec. 4.2) and reaches 96.3% token-state usage (Fig. 2).
Scope and assumptions:

The static baseline is max-length reservation, like Kwon’s “Orca (Max)”. It is modeled with no external fragmentation because every slot has the same size, although Kwon et al. still attribute 8.9% of Orca (Max) KV memory to external fragmentation and other overhead. Exact-size and power-of-two contiguous allocators, which trade reservation waste for external fragmentation, are not modeled.
Both allocators are sized with every admitted request at its full length (peak occupancy). A request mid-generation holds fewer paged blocks, so paged capacity is conservative, while static reserves max_seq_len for the whole request lifetime either way.
Request lengths are exponential, cut off at max_seq_len, with mean mean_request_tokens (calc_capped_exponential_scale).

Literature Source: 1. Kwon et al. (2023), “Efficient Memory Management for Large Language Model Serving with PagedAttention,” SOSP ’23. 2. Yu et al. (2022), “ORCA: A Distributed Serving System for Transformer-Based Generative Models.”





Name
Description




solve
Compare static max-length KV reservation with paged allocation.





solvers.ContinuousBatchingModel.solve(
    model,
    hardware,
    max_seq_len,
    mean_request_tokens=None,
    max_batch_size=1,
    page_size=16,
    precision='fp16',
    efficiency=0.5,
)
Compare static max-length KV reservation with paged allocation.
With KV budget M_KV (HBM capacity minus weights) and k KV bytes per token:

Static reservation: every request reserves max_seq_len tokens, so N_static = floor(M_KV / (k * S_max)) and the unused share of each reservation is 1 - S_mean / S_max.
Paged allocation: the budget is a pool of floor(M_KV / (k * p)) blocks and a request of S tokens holds ceil(S / p) of them, so N_paged = floor(pool / E[ceil(S / p)]). The unused share is the expected tail of each request’s last block (calc_expected_paged_kv_tokens), which grows with page size.
Both counts are capped by max_batch_size. When the cap binds for both allocators, allocation policy cannot change throughput.
Throughput: decode is memory-bound and streams the weights once per step plus the KV tokens requests have actually filled (reserved but empty slots are not read), t_step = (W + N * S_mean * k) / BW and tokens/s = N / t_step. speedup_vs_static is the paged throughput over the static throughput, each at its own N.
TTFT is the worst-case prefill of a full scheduler batch (max_batch_size prompts of max_seq_len tokens): linear 2*P*S plus attention 4*L*H*d*S^2 FLOPs, plus the dispatch tax.

Type
Description
Default

required

required

required

None

title: engine.solvers.realtime
text:
engine.solvers.realtime
Real-time solvers: the timed path between a learned proposer and the drives.
Domain implementations behind mlsysim.solvers (the public import path, derived from engine.solvers.__init__). The equations live in physics.robotics.control (phase lag of a delay, response-time bound, CAN FD and EtherCAT serialization, the lease ceiling) and physics.robotics.stopping; these models compose them for one stated situation (added 2026-10-20).





Name
Description




CanFdBusModel
Serialization occupancy of a cyclic CAN FD exchange: frames x t_frame against the cycle.


CommandAuthenticationModel
Authentication of a remote command as one more pre-brake delay, and a flood of forgeries.


EtherCatCycleModel
One EtherCAT summation frame through a chain of drives (calc_ethercat_cycle_time).


LeaseBudgetModel
A chunk lease as a term of the stopping budget, bounded by the lease rule.


PhaseLagBudgetModel
Phase a sampled loop spends on delay at its crossover frequency.


ResponseTimeModel
Response-time bound of one periodic task, R = C + B + I, against its deadline.


SharedDramReadModel
A permission tick’s snapshot read behind FIFO backlogs on a shared DRAM controller.


ThermalThrottleModel
A tick on a governed clock: a thermal trip halves the clock until the junction clears.





engine.solvers.realtime.CanFdBusModel()
Serialization occupancy of a cyclic CAN FD exchange: frames x t_frame against the cycle.
Frame time and bits come from calc_canfd_bus_utilization (ISO 11898-1:2015 frame format, worst-case stuffing by default). Occupancy is a necessary check only; blocking and retransmission need a response-time analysis. axes_capacity is the most axes whose frames fit one cycle.



engine.solvers.realtime.CommandAuthenticationModel()
Authentication of a remote command as one more pre-brake delay, and a flood of forgeries.
A published cycle count divided by the permission processor’s clock gives the time of one signature verification and of a MAC over a frame of mac_blocks cipher blocks. Verification adds to the delay before a remote stop can act, so each millisecond is travel at speed against the finished budget’s spare; a replay at the edge of the freshness window carries the machine v x tau_fresh. Verified serially, n forged signed packets queued ahead of a genuine veto finish it at (n + 1) t_verify; the fewest that push it past the deadline is n = floor(T_latest / t_verify), sustained at n / ((n + 1) t_verify) packets per second (added 2026-10-20).



engine.solvers.realtime.EtherCatCycleModel()
One EtherCAT summation frame through a chain of drives (calc_ethercat_cycle_time).
The frame carries every axis’s process data; each node forwards it with a fixed hop delay, so occupancy is serialization plus forwarding.



engine.solvers.realtime.LeaseBudgetModel()
A chunk lease as a term of the stopping budget, bounded by the lease rule.
After the last admission a stalled proposer’s chunk drives on for the lease; the tick that notices expiry and the bus cycle that carries the stop follow, then the brake onset. That interval is travel at speed, added to the braking travel, the localization and margin overhead, and the onset travel (StoppingBudgetModel). The lease rule bounds the lease from both sides:
T_renew + T_jitter  <  T_lease  <=  tau_max - T_tick - T_bus - T_onset - age
where tau_max is the longest pre-brake delay whose stop fits and age is the evidence’s age when the chunk is admitted. The stall timeline puts the stall after the second renewal completes.



engine.solvers.realtime.PhaseLagBudgetModel()
Phase a sampled loop spends on delay at its crossover frequency.
The hold costs half a sample period, then the compute and transport delays; a pure delay tau removes 360 f_c tau degrees at crossover (calc_phase_lag_total). Against a stated phase allowance the model also gives the largest total delay the allowance absorbs and the highest crossover the delay supports. A budget, not a stability proof.



engine.solvers.realtime.ResponseTimeModel()
Response-time bound of one periodic task, R = C + B + I, against its deadline.
calc_response_time_bound sums the declared WCET, the blocking bound, and the interference bound; the margin and the largest blocking that still meets the deadline follow. With an observed unloaded run, the gap between it and the declared WCET is the claim that timing analysis must justify.



engine.solvers.realtime.SharedDramReadModel()
A permission tick’s snapshot read behind FIFO backlogs on a shared DRAM controller.
One backlog (a weight tile, a camera transfer, and a telemetry record, at AXI transaction granularity) waits bytes / bandwidth plus its row conflicts (calc_axi_fifo_contention); the tick’s snapshot read follows. Against the sense allowance, the declared WCET, and the execution ceiling (deadline less blocking and interference), each less the compute after sensing, the model counts the most whole backlogs that still fit and the tick’s end time at each count. A FIFO controller is optimistic: a row-hit-first controller can keep passing the read.



engine.solvers.realtime.ThermalThrottleModel()
A tick on a governed clock: a thermal trip halves the clock until the junction clears.
The tick is sized to its declared WCET at the nominal clock; the throttled clock stretches the same cycles. The junction is a first-order lumped model, T(t) = T_inf - (T_inf - T_0) exp(-t / tau) with steady state T_amb + P theta; the clock returns only at the clear threshold, so the hysteresis lasts tau ln((T_trip - T_quiet) / (T_clear - T_quiet)) after the load stops (calc_first_order_time_to_temperature).

title: engine.solvers.curation
text:
engine.solvers.curation
Trajectory curation solvers: what a recorded corpus may teach, and what collecting it costs.
Domain implementations behind mlsysim.solvers (added 2026-10-20). Each model is arithmetic on stated counts, rates, and service times: failures that counterfactual probes attribute to the system, and the price of training on all of them anyway; how often a random split of runs places one task on both sides; the expected checking time of an admission route run in different orders; one record class’s share of a pool under three denominators; and how fast a verifier timeout burst fills reserved staging.





Name
Description




AdmissionOrderModel
One admission route’s independent checks run in different orders, each stopping at its first failure.


CorpusDenominatorsModel
One record class’s share of a retained pool counted three ways: records, stored tokens, selected targets.


FailureTriageModel
Failures that counterfactual probes remove below the weights, and the price of training on all of them.


RunSplitLeakageModel
Tasks whose runs a random split of runs places on both sides of the partition.


StagingBurstModel
Reserved staging under a verifier timeout burst, with every record charged at its ceiling.





engine.solvers.curation.AdmissionOrderModel()
One admission route’s independent checks run in different orders, each stopping at its first failure.
Every order admits the same records (the route yield is the product of the pass rates); the expected slot time per attempted record differs. Time per admitted record divides by the yield. The saving compares the cheapest order with the dearest.



engine.solvers.curation.CorpusDenominatorsModel()
One record class’s share of a retained pool counted three ways: records, stored tokens, selected targets.
Each class gives (records, stored tokens per record, selected target tokens per record). The admitted-token share counts stored tokens only over the classes the route admits.



engine.solvers.curation.FailureTriageModel()
Failures that counterfactual probes remove below the weights, and the price of training on all of them.
runs x failure_rate failures; each probe removes its share (rounded to whole failures), and the rest survive every probe. Training on every failure for epochs epochs of sequence_tokens costs 6PD FLOPs, run on devices at peak_rate x utilization and billed per device-hour.



engine.solvers.curation.RunSplitLeakageModel()
Tasks whose runs a random split of runs places on both sides of the partition.
Each run goes to training with probability f. A task with k runs straddles with probability 1 - f^k - (1 - f)^k; a test run has a sibling in training unless all k - 1 siblings also went to test. The majority count is the smallest k at which more than half the tasks straddle.



engine.solvers.curation.StagingBurstModel()
Reserved staging under a verifier timeout burst, with every record charged at its ceiling.
Rollouts finish at rollouts / rollout_time; verifiers serve slots / mean_service nominally and slots / timeout once every check runs to its timeout. The difference, times the record ceiling, fills the store. Stopping dispatch leaves the running rollouts and the growth during the controller’s reaction delay, so dispatch must stop at or below 1 - (in flight + reaction growth) / store.
