Type
Description





Quantity
Distance in meters.

title: physics.statistics
text:
physics.statistics
Statistical and workflow propagation helpers.





Name
Description




calc_arcsine_two_arm_sample_size
Runs per arm to detect Cohen’s h two-sided at alpha with power.


calc_behavior_cloning_cost_bound
Worst-case excess cost of behavioral cloning over horizon_steps: S^2 eps.


calc_cdf_quantile
First value whose empirical cumulative fraction reaches fraction.


calc_chance_agreement
Agreement two independent annotators reach by chance: sum_k s_k ** 2.


calc_chi2_gate
Chi-square quantile that a consistent statistic with dof degrees of freedom stays below with probability confidence (added 2026-10-20).


calc_chi2_mean_band
Two-sided acceptance band for the mean of n_samples consistent chi-square statistics (added 2026-10-20).


calc_chi_square_quantile
Quantile of the chi-square distribution: the squared Mahalanobis radius of a Gaussian


calc_clopper_pearson_interval
Exact two-sided Clopper-Pearson interval for successes out of trials.


calc_cohens_h
Cohen’s effect size for two proportions: h = 2 asin sqrt(p1) - 2 asin sqrt(p2) (Cohen 1988, ch. 6).


calc_cohens_kappa
Cohen’s kappa: agreement beyond chance, (p_o - p_e) / (1 - p_e) (Cohen 1960).


calc_conjunctive_confidence
Confidence in a claim that needs every one of several independent premises.


calc_consecutive_detection_frames
Consecutive frames a person must be in view before detection may be counted on.


calc_cross_entropy_exponential_proposal
Expected (large-sample) cross-entropy iteration for an exponential tail.


calc_dagger_cost_bound
Worst-case excess cost with expert labels on learner states: u S eps.


calc_effective_sample_size
Effective number of independent samples in n_records of an AR(1) series.


calc_equal_n_for_z
Per-group sample size at which the pooled two-proportion z of a fixed gap reaches z_critical.


calc_expected_calibration_error
Expected calibration error of binned predictions: sum \|B_i\| / n * \|acc_i - conf_i\|.


calc_exponential_decay_rate
Rate gamma of A(t) = A0 exp(-gamma t) through two readings:


calc_fisher_exact_two_sided
Two-sided Fisher exact p for the 2x2 table [[a, b], [c, d]] (rows are the two arms).


calc_gaussian_kl
KL divergence KL(P \|\| Q) between two normal distributions, in nats.


calc_gaussian_kl_terms
The two terms of KL(P \|\| Q) for normals P and Q.


calc_importance_sampling_exponential
Importance-sampling statistics for an exponential tail with an exponential proposal.


calc_jensen_shannon_divergence
Jensen-Shannon divergence between two aligned distributions, in nats.


calc_ks_coefficient
Large-sample two-sample K-S coefficient c(alpha) = sqrt(-ln(alpha / 2) / 2).


calc_ks_critical_value
Large-sample two-sample Kolmogorov-Smirnov critical value.


calc_ks_normal_location_shift
K-S distance between two equal-variance normals whose means differ by shift_sd sds.


calc_linf_corner_l2
Euclidean length of a corner of the l-infinity ball of radius linf_budget in coordinates dimensions.


calc_mcnemar_exact_two_sided
Exact two-sided McNemar p from the discordant counts (McNemar 1947).


calc_mcnemar_max_discordant
Largest disagreement count b + c at which McNemar’s statistic still exceeds critical.


calc_mean_half_width
Half-width of a confidence interval on a mean of n_samples values: t_{n-1} sd / sqrt(n).


calc_monte_carlo_sample_size
Plain Monte Carlo draws needed to estimate a probability to a relative error.


calc_multilegged_confidence
Confidence in a claim supported by independent legs, any one of which suffices.


calc_newcombe_paired_difference
Paired difference of two acceptance rates with Newcombe’s method-10 interval (Newcombe 1998).


calc_noncentral_gate_detection
Probability that a biased innovation’s NIS exceeds gate (added 2026-10-20).


calc_one_proportion_sample_size
Outcomes a one-sample binomial test needs to tell alternative_rate from null_rate.


calc_optimal_exponential_proposal_mean
Mean of the exponential proposal that minimizes importance-sampling variance.


calc_paired_difference_variance
Per-pair variance of a paired candidate-minus-baseline outcome in {-1, 0, +1}: d - delta^2.


calc_poisson_exact_interval
Exact (Garwood) two-sided 1 - alpha interval on a Poisson mean after events events.


calc_poisson_mean_for_reserve
Largest Poisson mean at which reserve still holds P(N >= reserve) below target.


calc_poisson_reserve
Smallest reserve s whose Poisson tail P(N >= s) is below target.


calc_poisson_tail
P(N >= s) for N ~ Poisson(mean): 1 - sum_{k<s} e^-m m^k / k!.


calc_population_stability_index
Population Stability Index (PSI) between two aligned distributions.


calc_proportion_gap_interval
Normal-approximation interval of a gap rate_a - rate_b (unpooled standard error).


calc_proportion_gap_se
Unpooled standard error of a gap rate_a - rate_b between two independent groups (added 2026-10-20).


calc_proportion_half_width
Normal-approximation half-width of a proportion from n_samples independent draws: z sqrt(p (1 - p) / n).


calc_sample_collection_time
Time for a traffic slice to collect samples observations (added 2026-10-20).


calc_samples_for_half_width
Independent draws for a normal-approximation half-width at rate: ceil(z^2 p (1 - p) / h^2).


calc_samples_per_arm_for_difference
Samples per arm for a two-sided two-sample test of a mean difference: 2 (z_a + z_b)^2 sd^2 / d^2.


calc_smoothing_radius
Binary randomized-smoothing certified l2 radius sigma * Phi^-1(p_A) (Cohen et al. 2019).


calc_spearman_rank_correlation
Spearman’s rank correlation: Pearson correlation of the average ranks (ties share a rank).


calc_split_conformal_min_count
Fewest calibration scores for which the split-conformal rank exists (added 2026-10-20).


calc_split_conformal_rank
Rank of the sorted calibration score that bounds new scores at level 1 - alpha (added 2026-10-20).


calc_sprt_boundaries
Wald’s accept and reject boundaries on the log-likelihood ratio: ln((1-b)/a), ln(b/(1-a)).


calc_sprt_expected_samples
Wald’s expected stopping sample count, neglecting overshoot.


calc_sprt_increments
Wald SPRT log-likelihood increments per success and per failure, failure-probability convention.


calc_standard_error
Standard error of a mean of n_samples independent values with spread sd: sd / sqrt(n).


calc_t_critical
Two-sided Student t critical value: the (1 + confidence) / 2 quantile (2.78 at 4 dof, 0.95).


calc_task_averaged_variance
Variance of a task-averaged acceptance estimate: sigma_task^2 / N + sigma_run^2 / (N r).


calc_two_proportion_detectable_lift
Smallest absolute lift a two-arm test with n_per_variant per arm can detect.


calc_two_proportion_sample_size
Per-arm sample size for a two-proportion A/B test.


calc_two_proportion_z
Pooled two-proportion z statistic for an observed gap rate_a - rate_b.


calc_wald_interval
Wald interval for a binomial proportion: p_hat +/- z sqrt(p_hat (1 - p_hat) / n).


calc_welch_interval
Welch’s interval on mean_a - mean_b for two samples with unequal spreads (Welch 1947).


calc_wilson_clean_runs
Fewest consecutive clean runs whose Wilson upper limit on the failure rate falls below target_upper.


calc_wilson_interval
Wilson score interval for a binomial proportion (Wilson 1927), clipped to [0, 1].


calc_within_task_variance
Mean within-task run variance E[p_i (1 - p_i)] = mean (1 - mean) - Var(p_i).


fit_exponential_growth
Least-squares fit of log10(y) on x; growth factor per period of x.





physics.statistics.calc_arcsine_two_arm_sample_size(
    effect_h,
    alpha=0.05,
    power=0.8,
)
Runs per arm to detect Cohen’s h two-sided at alpha with power.
Each arcsine-transformed fraction has variance 1/n, so a difference of two arms has variance 2/n: n = ceil(2 ((z_{1-a/2} + z_power) / h)^2) (Cohen 1988, Table 6.4.1 lists 392 per arm at h = 0.2).



physics.statistics.calc_behavior_cloning_cost_bound(
    horizon_steps,
    per_step_error,
)
Worst-case excess cost of behavioral cloning over horizon_steps: S^2 eps.
Ross and Bagnell (2010), Theorem 2.1: a policy trained only on the demonstrator’s states compounds a per-step error eps quadratically.



physics.statistics.calc_cdf_quantile(values, cumulative, fraction)
First value whose empirical cumulative fraction reaches fraction.
values ascend with cumulative (a released CDF); past the end the last value is returned.



physics.statistics.calc_chance_agreement(class_shares)
Agreement two independent annotators reach by chance: sum_k s_k ** 2.
class_shares is each annotator’s label mix (fractions summing to 1); both annotators are assumed to share it.



physics.statistics.calc_chi2_gate(confidence, dof)
Chi-square quantile that a consistent statistic with dof degrees of freedom stays below with probability confidence (added 2026-10-20).
A validation gate rejects an innovation whose normalized squared value (NIS) exceeds this threshold.
Source: Bar-Shalom, Li, and Kirubarajan, Estimation with Applications to Tracking and Navigation (2001), Sec. 5.4.



physics.statistics.calc_chi2_mean_band(n_samples, dof, confidence)
Two-sided acceptance band for the mean of n_samples consistent chi-square statistics (added 2026-10-20).
The sum of N independent NEES (or NIS) values of dimension n is chi-square with N n degrees of freedom; dividing its central confidence interval by N gives the band the sample mean must fall in.
Source: Bar-Shalom, Li, and Kirubarajan (2001), Sec. 5.4.2.



physics.statistics.calc_chi_square_quantile(degrees_of_freedom, coverage)
Quantile of the chi-square distribution: the squared Mahalanobis radius of a Gaussian confidence region holding probability coverage in degrees_of_freedom dimensions (added 2026-10-20).
A point of a k-dimensional Gaussian lies inside the region (x - mu)^T Sigma^-1 (x - mu) <= r^2 with probability coverage when r^2 is this quantile; the region’s principal semi-axes are r sigma_i. For k = 3 and 0.95 the quantile is about 7.815.
Source: the chi-square distribution of a sum of k squared standard normals (NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook of Statistical Methods, Sec. 1.3.6.6.6).



physics.statistics.calc_clopper_pearson_interval(
    successes,
    trials,
    confidence=0.95,
)
Exact two-sided Clopper-Pearson interval for successes out of trials.
Equation (beta quantiles, alpha = 1 - confidence): lower = B^{-1}(alpha/2; k, n - k + 1) (0 when k = 0) upper = B^{-1}(1 - alpha/2; k + 1, n - k) (1 when k = n)
Source: Clopper and Pearson, “The Use of Confidence or Fiducial Limits Illustrated in the Case of the Binomial,” Biometrika 26(4), 1934.



physics.statistics.calc_cohens_h(p_high, p_low)
Cohen’s effect size for two proportions: h = 2 asin sqrt(p1) - 2 asin sqrt(p2) (Cohen 1988, ch. 6).



physics.statistics.calc_cohens_kappa(observed_agreement, chance_agreement)
Cohen’s kappa: agreement beyond chance, (p_o - p_e) / (1 - p_e) (Cohen 1960).



physics.statistics.calc_conjunctive_confidence(premise_confidences)
Confidence in a claim that needs every one of several independent premises.
Equation: P(claim) = prod_i p_i
The conjunction is no stronger than its weakest premise and, with more than one premise below 1, strictly weaker.
Source: probability of the intersection of independent events, as applied to conjunctive assurance arguments in Bloomfield and Littlewood 2003, “Multi-legged arguments: the impact of diversity upon confidence in dependability arguments” (DSN 2003).



physics.statistics.calc_consecutive_detection_frames(
    per_frame_detection,
    all_miss_probability,
)
Consecutive frames a person must be in view before detection may be counted on.
Equation: N = ceil( ln p_miss / ln(1 - p_frame) )
the fewest frames for which the chance of missing the person in every one, (1 - p_frame)^N, is at most all_miss_probability, with misses independent from frame to frame (the best case; correlated misses need more frames). A tolerance of 1e-12 keeps an exact ratio from rounding up.



physics.statistics.calc_cross_entropy_exponential_proposal(
    threshold,
    operational_mean,
    elite_share,
)
Expected (large-sample) cross-entropy iteration for an exponential tail.
From q_0 = p = Exp(m0), each round sets the level to the (1 - beta) quantile of the current proposal, level = -m_k ln(beta) (capped at the threshold), and refits the proposal mean to the likelihood-weighted elite draws; for this family that is E_p[D | D > level] = level + m0. Stops when the level reaches the threshold, so the final mean is threshold + m0.
Returns a dict with levels (list, in the units of threshold), n_levels, and proposal_mean.
Source: Rubinstein and Kroese, The Cross-Entropy Method (Springer, 2004), multilevel rare-event algorithm; the exponential refit is in closed form.



physics.statistics.calc_dagger_cost_bound(
    horizon_steps,
    per_step_error,
    recoverability=1.0,
)
Worst-case excess cost with expert labels on learner states: u S eps.
Ross, Gordon, and Bagnell (2011), Theorem 3.2: linear in the horizon while the recoverability constant u stays bounded.



physics.statistics.calc_effective_sample_size(n_records, lag1_correlation)
Effective number of independent samples in n_records of an AR(1) series.
N_eff = N (1 - rho) / (1 + rho) for estimating the mean of a series whose adjacent records have lag-one correlation rho (Thiebaux and Zwiers 1984).



physics.statistics.calc_equal_n_for_z(rate_a, rate_b, z_critical)
Per-group sample size at which the pooled two-proportion z of a fixed gap reaches z_critical.
With equal groups, z = gap / sqrt(2 p (1 - p) / n), so n = 2 p (1 - p) (z_critical / gap)^2 with p the mean of the two rates.



physics.statistics.calc_expected_calibration_error(bins)
Expected calibration error of binned predictions: sum |B_i| / n * |acc_i - conf_i|.
bins is a sequence of (count, confidence, accuracy); the weight of each bin is its share of the predictions (Pakdaman Naeini et al. 2015; Guo et al. 2017, eq. 3).



physics.statistics.calc_exponential_decay_rate(initial, later, elapsed)
Rate gamma of A(t) = A0 exp(-gamma t) through two readings: gamma = ln(A0 / A1) / t. elapsed may be a Quantity (the rate is then per its unit) or a plain number.



physics.statistics.calc_fisher_exact_two_sided(a, b, c, d)
Two-sided Fisher exact p for the 2x2 table [[a, b], [c, d]] (rows are the two arms).
Sums the hypergeometric probabilities of every table with the observed margins that is no more probable than the observed one. Source: Fisher, Statistical Methods for Research Workers (1934 ed.), sec. 21.02.



physics.statistics.calc_gaussian_kl(mean_p, sd_p, mean_q, sd_q)
KL divergence KL(P || Q) between two normal distributions, in nats.



physics.statistics.calc_gaussian_kl_terms(mean_p, sd_p, mean_q, sd_q)
The two terms of KL(P || Q) for normals P and Q.
KL = ln(sd_q / sd_p) + (sd_p^2 + (mean_p - mean_q)^2) / (2 sd_q^2) - 1/2. Returns (log_term, ratio_numerator, ratio_denominator) so a worked example can show each piece; calc_gaussian_kl adds them.



physics.statistics.calc_importance_sampling_exponential(
    threshold,
    operational_mean,
    proposal_mean,
)
Importance-sampling statistics for an exponential tail with an exponential proposal.
Operational model p = Exp(mean m0), failure when D > gamma, proposal q = Exp(mean m_q) with likelihood ratio w = p/q. Writing lam = 1/m0 and eta = 1/m_q (eta < 2 lam so the second moment is finite):
P_F                 = exp(-lam gamma)
E_q[w^2 1{D>gamma}] = lam^2 / (eta (2 lam - eta)) * exp(-(2 lam - eta) gamma)
relative variance   = E_q[w^2 1{D>gamma}] / P_F^2 - 1      (per draw)
ESS per draw        = E_q[w]^2 / E_q[w^2] = eta (2 lam - eta) / lam^2
P_q(D > gamma)      = exp(-eta gamma)
Draws for a relative standard error r are relative_variance / r**2. threshold, operational_mean, and proposal_mean are Pint quantities of one dimension (or plain floats in one unit).
Source: likelihood-ratio estimator, its second moment, and the effective sample size (sum w)^2 / sum w^2 from Owen 2013, ch. 9; the exponential closed forms follow by integrating those expressions.



physics.statistics.calc_jensen_shannon_divergence(p, q)
Jensen-Shannon divergence between two aligned distributions, in nats.
JS = KL(p || m) / 2 + KL(q || m) / 2 with m = (p + q) / 2. It is symmetric and bounded by ln 2, which two distributions with disjoint support reach. Source: Lin, “Divergence Measures Based on the Shannon Entropy,” IEEE Trans. Inf. Theory 37(1), 1991.



physics.statistics.calc_ks_coefficient(significance)
Large-sample two-sample K-S coefficient c(alpha) = sqrt(-ln(alpha / 2) / 2).
About 1.36 at 0.05 (Ops.Monitoring.KsTestCoefficient) and 1.63 at 0.01; calc_ks_critical_value scales it by the two sample sizes.



physics.statistics.calc_ks_critical_value(coefficient, n_reference, n_current)
Large-sample two-sample Kolmogorov-Smirnov critical value.
D_crit = c * sqrt((n_0 + n_t) / (n_0 * n_t)), where c is the coefficient for the chosen significance level (1.36 at 0.05, Ops.Monitoring.KsTestCoefficient).



physics.statistics.calc_ks_normal_location_shift(shift_sd)
K-S distance between two equal-variance normals whose means differ by shift_sd sds.
The CDF gap is largest midway between the means: 2 * Phi(shift_sd / 2) - 1, which equals erf(shift_sd / (2 * sqrt(2))).



physics.statistics.calc_linf_corner_l2(linf_budget, coordinates)
Euclidean length of a corner of the l-infinity ball of radius linf_budget in coordinates dimensions.



physics.statistics.calc_mcnemar_exact_two_sided(first_only, second_only)
Exact two-sided McNemar p from the discordant counts (McNemar 1947).
Conditional on d = first_only + second_only discordant pairs, wins are Binomial(d, 1/2) under equal marginals: p = min(1, 2 sum_{j <= min(b, c)} C(d, j) 2^-d); 1 when d = 0.



physics.statistics.calc_mcnemar_max_discordant(net_gap, critical)
Largest disagreement count b + c at which McNemar’s statistic still exceeds critical.
The statistic (no continuity correction) is (b - c)^2 / (b + c); with the net gap b - c fixed, it exceeds the 1-dof chi-square critical value only when b + c <= floor(gap^2 / critical) (McNemar 1947).



physics.statistics.calc_mean_half_width(sd, n_samples, confidence)
Half-width of a confidence interval on a mean of n_samples values: t_{n-1} sd / sqrt(n).



physics.statistics.calc_monte_carlo_sample_size(
    failure_probability,
    relative_error,
)
Plain Monte Carlo draws needed to estimate a probability to a relative error.
Equation: N = (1 - p) / (p * r^2)
The binomial estimator p_hat = k/N has relative standard error sqrt((1 - p) / (N p)); solving for N at a target r gives the count.
Source: Owen, Monte Carlo Theory, Methods and Examples (2013): the variance of a sample mean of Bernoulli draws, as used for rare events in ch. 9.



physics.statistics.calc_multilegged_confidence(leg_confidences)
Confidence in a claim supported by independent legs, any one of which suffices.
Equation: P(claim) = 1 - prod_i (1 - p_i)
Holds only if the legs fail independently; common-cause failure collapses the legs back into a conjunction.
Source: Bloomfield and Littlewood 2003 (DSN), multi-legged arguments under the independence assumption.



physics.statistics.calc_newcombe_paired_difference(
    both,
    first_only,
    second_only,
    neither,
    z_critical,
)
Paired difference of two acceptance rates with Newcombe’s method-10 interval (Newcombe 1998).
The four cells count the tasks both configurations accept, only the first, only the second, and neither. Returns (delta, low, high) for the first configuration’s rate minus the second’s. Each marginal Wilson interval is combined through the continuity-corrected phi of the 2x2 table, so positive within-pair dependence narrows the interval.



physics.statistics.calc_noncentral_gate_detection(gate, dof, noncentrality)
Probability that a biased innovation’s NIS exceeds gate (added 2026-10-20).
A bias b in an innovation of variance S makes its NIS noncentral chi-square with noncentrality b^2 / S, so its mean is dof + b^2 / S; a single-update gate catches it only with this probability.
Source: Bar-Shalom, Li, and Kirubarajan (2001), Sec. 1.4.17 (noncentral chi-square) and Sec. 5.4.



physics.statistics.calc_one_proportion_sample_size(
    null_rate,
    alternative_rate,
    z_alpha,
    z_beta,
)
Outcomes a one-sample binomial test needs to tell alternative_rate from null_rate.
Normal approximation with the variance of each hypothesis on its own side: n = ((z_alpha sqrt(p0 (1 - p0)) + z_beta sqrt(p1 (1 - p1))) / (p0 - p1))^2. The count grows as one over the squared gap, so halving the gap needs about four times the outcomes.



physics.statistics.calc_optimal_exponential_proposal_mean(
    threshold,
    operational_mean,
)
Mean of the exponential proposal that minimizes importance-sampling variance.
Minimizing the second moment of calc_importance_sampling_exponential over eta gives the root below 2 lam of
gamma eta^2 - (2 + 2 lam gamma) eta + 2 lam = 0,
and the proposal mean is 1/eta. Returned in the units of threshold.
Source: first-order condition on the exponential second moment (Owen 2013, ch. 9, exponential tilting of a light-tailed tail).



physics.statistics.calc_paired_difference_variance(
    discordant_fraction,
    difference,
)
Per-pair variance of a paired candidate-minus-baseline outcome in {-1, 0, +1}: d - delta^2.



physics.statistics.calc_poisson_exact_interval(events, alpha=0.05)
Exact (Garwood) two-sided 1 - alpha interval on a Poisson mean after events events.
Solves the Poisson tails P(N >= k) = alpha/2 (lower) and P(N <= k) = alpha/2 (upper) by bisection. Divide by the exposure to get a rate interval. Source: Garwood, “Fiducial Limits for the Poisson Distribution,” Biometrika 28(3/4), 1936.



physics.statistics.calc_poisson_mean_for_reserve(reserve, target, iterations=60)
Largest Poisson mean at which reserve still holds P(N >= reserve) below target.
Bisection on the tail, which rises monotonically with the mean.



physics.statistics.calc_poisson_reserve(mean, target)
Smallest reserve s whose Poisson tail P(N >= s) is below target.



physics.statistics.calc_poisson_tail(mean, at_least)
P(N >= s) for N ~ Poisson(mean): 1 - sum_{k<s} e^-m m^k / k!.
The chance that at least s events fall in an interval whose expected count is mean; 1 for s <= 0. A pool with s standby instances and a constant replenishment lead time misses a request exactly when at least s earlier replacements are still outstanding.



physics.statistics.calc_population_stability_index(
    expected,
    actual,
    epsilon=1e-12,
)
Population Stability Index (PSI) between two aligned distributions.
Measures distribution drift between a reference (“expected”) and an observed (“actual”) binned distribution: PSI = sum_i (actual_i - expected_i) * ln(actual_i / expected_i) (the symmetrized KL divergence). Interpretation thresholds live in Ops.Monitoring (the single source of truth the book follows: 0.10 warn / 0.20 review / 0.25 critical) — do not restate bands here.











Name
Type
Description
Default




expected
sequence of float
Bin probabilities (dimensionless, each summing to ~1), aligned bin-for-bin and of equal length.
required


actual
sequence of float
Bin probabilities (dimensionless, each summing to ~1), aligned bin-for-bin and of equal length.
required


epsilon
float
Floor applied to every bin to avoid log(0) / division by zero when a bin is empty.
1e-12














Name
Type
Description





float
PSI value (dimensionless, >= 0; 0 means identical distributions).







physics.statistics.calc_proportion_gap_interval(
    rate_a,
    rate_b,
    n_a,
    n_b,
    z_critical,
)
Normal-approximation interval of a gap rate_a - rate_b (unpooled standard error).
Returns (low, high): the gap minus and plus z_critical standard errors, se = sqrt(p_a (1 - p_a) / n_a + p_b (1 - p_b) / n_b).



physics.statistics.calc_proportion_gap_se(rate_a, rate_b, n_a, n_b)
Unpooled standard error of a gap rate_a - rate_b between two independent groups (added 2026-10-20).
se = sqrt(p_a (1 - p_a) / n_a + p_b (1 - p_b) / n_b).



physics.statistics.calc_proportion_half_width(rate, n_samples, z_critical)
Normal-approximation half-width of a proportion from n_samples independent draws: z sqrt(p (1 - p) / n).



physics.statistics.calc_sample_collection_time(
    samples,
    request_rate,
    traffic_share,
)
Time for a traffic slice to collect samples observations (added 2026-10-20).
A canary stage that receives traffic_share of request_rate gathers its planned guardrail sample in t = n / (r p).



physics.statistics.calc_samples_for_half_width(rate, half_width, z_critical)
Independent draws for a normal-approximation half-width at rate: ceil(z^2 p (1 - p) / h^2).



physics.statistics.calc_samples_per_arm_for_difference(
    sd,
    difference,
    z_alpha,
    z_beta,
)
Samples per arm for a two-sided two-sample test of a mean difference: 2 (z_a + z_b)^2 sd^2 / d^2.
The normal-approximation power formula; z_alpha is the two-sided critical value (1.96 at 95 percent) and z_beta the power quantile (0.84 at 80 percent power). Not rounded up.



physics.statistics.calc_smoothing_radius(noise_sd, top_class_probability)
Binary randomized-smoothing certified l2 radius sigma * Phi^-1(p_A) (Cohen et al. 2019).



physics.statistics.calc_spearman_rank_correlation(xs, ys)
Spearman’s rank correlation: Pearson correlation of the average ranks (ties share a rank).



physics.statistics.calc_split_conformal_min_count(alpha)
Fewest calibration scores for which the split-conformal rank exists (added 2026-10-20).
The rank ceil((n + 1)(1 - alpha)) must not exceed n, which holds from n = ceil((1 - alpha) / alpha).



physics.statistics.calc_split_conformal_rank(calibration_count, alpha)
Rank of the sorted calibration score that bounds new scores at level 1 - alpha (added 2026-10-20).
Split conformal prediction takes the ceil((n + 1)(1 - alpha))-th smallest of n exchangeable calibration scores; a new score exceeds it with probability at most alpha. A rank above n means the calibration set is too small to state the bound.
Source: Angelopoulos and Bates, “Conformal Prediction: A Gentle Introduction,” Found. Trends Mach. Learn. 16(4), 2023, Sec. 1.



physics.statistics.calc_sprt_boundaries(alpha, beta)
Wald’s accept and reject boundaries on the log-likelihood ratio: ln((1-b)/a), ln(b/(1-a)).
alpha is the allowed false acceptance of H1 under H0 and beta the allowed false rejection of H1 under H1 (Wald 1945).



physics.statistics.calc_sprt_expected_samples(
    upper,
    lower,
    drift,
    upper_probability,
)
Wald’s expected stopping sample count, neglecting overshoot.
The walk ends at upper with probability upper_probability and at lower otherwise; dividing the expected terminal log-likelihood by the expected step drift gives E[N] (Wald 1945, average sample number).



physics.statistics.calc_sprt_increments(p_unacceptable, p_acceptable)
Wald SPRT log-likelihood increments per success and per failure, failure-probability convention.
With per-trial failure probability p0 under H0 (unacceptable) and p1 under H1 (acceptable), a success adds ln((1 - p1)/(1 - p0)) and a failure adds ln(p1/p0) to the log-likelihood ratio of H1 over H0. Source: Wald, “Sequential Tests of Statistical Hypotheses,” Ann. Math. Statist. 16(2), 1945.



physics.statistics.calc_standard_error(sd, n_samples)
Standard error of a mean of n_samples independent values with spread sd: sd / sqrt(n).



physics.statistics.calc_t_critical(degrees_of_freedom, confidence)
Two-sided Student t critical value: the (1 + confidence) / 2 quantile (2.78 at 4 dof, 0.95).
Non-integer degrees of freedom (Welch-Satterthwaite) are allowed.



physics.statistics.calc_task_averaged_variance(
    between_task_variance,
    within_task_variance,
    tasks,
    runs_per_task,
)
Variance of a task-averaged acceptance estimate: sigma_task^2 / N + sigma_run^2 / (N r).
Tasks are sampled independently and runs are independent given the task; more runs shrink only the second term, more tasks shrink both.



physics.statistics.calc_two_proportion_detectable_lift(
    baseline_rate,
    n_per_variant,
    z_alpha=1.96,
    z_beta=0.84,
)
Smallest absolute lift a two-arm test with n_per_variant per arm can detect.
The common-variance sample-size formula of calc_two_proportion_sample_size solved for the effect: delta = sqrt(2 (z_alpha + z_beta)^2 p (1 - p) / n).



physics.statistics.calc_two_proportion_sample_size(
    baseline_rate,
    detectable_lift,
    z_alpha=1.96,
    z_beta=0.84,
    pooled=False,
)
Per-arm sample size for a two-proportion A/B test.
Standard normal-approximation power formula: n = 2 * (z_alpha + z_beta)^2 * p(1-p) / delta^2, using the baseline rate’s variance for both arms (a common simplification valid for small lifts). Defaults correspond to a two-sided 5% significance level (z = 1.96) and 80% power (z = 0.84).











Name
Type
Description
Default




baseline_rate
float
Control-arm conversion rate p in (0, 1).
required


detectable_lift
float
Minimum absolute difference in rates to detect (same 0-1 scale as baseline_rate, e.g. 0.01 for one percentage point). Must be > 0.
required


z_alpha
float
Normal quantile for the significance level (1.96 = two-sided 0.05).
1.96


z_beta
float
Normal quantile for power (0.84 = 80% power).
0.84


pooled
bool
When True, use the pooled two-proportion form, which carries the variance of both arms rather than reusing the baseline’s for each: n = (z_alpha * sqrt(2 * p_bar * q_bar)        + z_beta * sqrt(p1*q1 + p2*q2))^2 / delta^2 where p_bar is the mean of the two rates. This is the textbook form and the one the book’s own appendix displays. It is not the default because the simplified form above is already in use and its results are quoted in print; pass pooled=True where the pooled form is the one being taught.
False














Name
Type
Description





float
Required sample size per arm (unrounded; callers should ceil).







physics.statistics.calc_two_proportion_z(rate_a, rate_b, n_a, n_b)
Pooled two-proportion z statistic for an observed gap rate_a - rate_b.
z = (p_a - p_b) / sqrt(p (1 - p) (1/n_a + 1/n_b)) with the pooled rate p = (n_a p_a + n_b p_b) / (n_a + n_b), the null hypothesis that both groups share one rate.



physics.statistics.calc_wald_interval(successes, trials, z_critical)
Wald interval for a binomial proportion: p_hat +/- z sqrt(p_hat (1 - p_hat) / n).
Not clipped to [0, 1], so near the boundaries it shows the impossible endpoints and the zero width at x = 0 or x = n that disqualify it (Brown, Cai, and DasGupta 2001).



physics.statistics.calc_welch_interval(
    mean_a,
    sd_a,
    n_a,
    mean_b,
    sd_b,
    n_b,
    confidence,
)
Welch’s interval on mean_a - mean_b for two samples with unequal spreads (Welch 1947).
se = sqrt(s_a^2 / n_a + s_b^2 / n_b); the Welch-Satterthwaite degrees of freedom are se^4 / ((s_a^2/n_a)^2 / (n_a - 1) + (s_b^2/n_b)^2 / (n_b - 1)). Returns dict(difference, se, dof, t, low, high).



physics.statistics.calc_wilson_clean_runs(target_upper, z)
Fewest consecutive clean runs whose Wilson upper limit on the failure rate falls below target_upper.
With zero failures in n runs the upper limit is z^2 / (n + z^2), which is below t once n > z^2 (1 - t) / t.



physics.statistics.calc_wilson_interval(successes, trials, z_critical)
Wilson score interval for a binomial proportion (Wilson 1927), clipped to [0, 1].
center = (x + z^2/2) / (n + z^2)
half   = z / (n + z^2) * sqrt(x (n - x) / n + z^2 / 4)
The variance uses the hypothesized rate, so the interval keeps a nonzero width at x = 0 and x = n and never leaves [0, 1].



physics.statistics.calc_within_task_variance(mean_rate, between_task_variance)
Mean within-task run variance E[p_i (1 - p_i)] = mean (1 - mean) - Var(p_i).



physics.statistics.fit_exponential_growth(xs, ys, period=1.0)
Least-squares fit of log10(y) on x; growth factor per period of x.
Returns (factor, slope, intercept) where log10(y) = intercept + slope * x and factor = 10 ** (slope * period). Trend lines on log-scale technology plots (compute, memory bandwidth, interconnect against year) are this fit.

calc_gaussian_kl_terms

calc_importance_sampling_exponential

calc_jensen_shannon_divergence

calc_ks_coefficient

calc_linf_corner_l2

calc_mcnemar_max_discordant

calc_population_stability_index

calc_proportion_gap_se

calc_sample_collection_time

physics.statistics.calc_arcsine_two_arm_sample_size(
    effect_h,
    alpha=0.05,
    power=0.8,
)
Runs per arm to detect Cohen’s h two-sided at alpha with power.
Each arcsine-transformed fraction has variance 1/n, so a difference of two arms has variance 2/n: n = ceil(2 ((z_{1-a/2} + z_power) / h)^2) (Cohen 1988, Table 6.4.1 lists 392 per arm at h = 0.2).



physics.statistics.calc_behavior_cloning_cost_bound(
    horizon_steps,
    per_step_error,
)
Worst-case excess cost of behavioral cloning over horizon_steps: S^2 eps.
Ross and Bagnell (2010), Theorem 2.1: a policy trained only on the demonstrator’s states compounds a per-step error eps quadratically.



physics.statistics.calc_cdf_quantile(values, cumulative, fraction)
First value whose empirical cumulative fraction reaches fraction.
values ascend with cumulative (a released CDF); past the end the last value is returned.



physics.statistics.calc_chance_agreement(class_shares)
Agreement two independent annotators reach by chance: sum_k s_k ** 2.
class_shares is each annotator’s label mix (fractions summing to 1); both annotators are assumed to share it.



physics.statistics.calc_chi2_gate(confidence, dof)
Chi-square quantile that a consistent statistic with dof degrees of freedom stays below with probability confidence (added 2026-10-20).
A validation gate rejects an innovation whose normalized squared value (NIS) exceeds this threshold.
Source: Bar-Shalom, Li, and Kirubarajan, Estimation with Applications to Tracking and Navigation (2001), Sec. 5.4.



physics.statistics.calc_chi2_mean_band(n_samples, dof, confidence)
Two-sided acceptance band for the mean of n_samples consistent chi-square statistics (added 2026-10-20).
The sum of N independent NEES (or NIS) values of dimension n is chi-square with N n degrees of freedom; dividing its central confidence interval by N gives the band the sample mean must fall in.
Source: Bar-Shalom, Li, and Kirubarajan (2001), Sec. 5.4.2.



physics.statistics.calc_chi_square_quantile(degrees_of_freedom, coverage)
Quantile of the chi-square distribution: the squared Mahalanobis radius of a Gaussian confidence region holding probability coverage in degrees_of_freedom dimensions (added 2026-10-20).
A point of a k-dimensional Gaussian lies inside the region (x - mu)^T Sigma^-1 (x - mu) <= r^2 with probability coverage when r^2 is this quantile; the region’s principal semi-axes are r sigma_i. For k = 3 and 0.95 the quantile is about 7.815.
Source: the chi-square distribution of a sum of k squared standard normals (NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook of Statistical Methods, Sec. 1.3.6.6.6).



physics.statistics.calc_clopper_pearson_interval(
    successes,
    trials,
    confidence=0.95,
)
Exact two-sided Clopper-Pearson interval for successes out of trials.
Equation (beta quantiles, alpha = 1 - confidence): lower = B^{-1}(alpha/2; k, n - k + 1) (0 when k = 0) upper = B^{-1}(1 - alpha/2; k + 1, n - k) (1 when k = n)
Source: Clopper and Pearson, “The Use of Confidence or Fiducial Limits Illustrated in the Case of the Binomial,” Biometrika 26(4), 1934.



physics.statistics.calc_cohens_h(p_high, p_low)
Cohen’s effect size for two proportions: h = 2 asin sqrt(p1) - 2 asin sqrt(p2) (Cohen 1988, ch. 6).



physics.statistics.calc_cohens_kappa(observed_agreement, chance_agreement)
Cohen’s kappa: agreement beyond chance, (p_o - p_e) / (1 - p_e) (Cohen 1960).



physics.statistics.calc_conjunctive_confidence(premise_confidences)
Confidence in a claim that needs every one of several independent premises.
Equation: P(claim) = prod_i p_i
The conjunction is no stronger than its weakest premise and, with more than one premise below 1, strictly weaker.
Source: probability of the intersection of independent events, as applied to conjunctive assurance arguments in Bloomfield and Littlewood 2003, “Multi-legged arguments: the impact of diversity upon confidence in dependability arguments” (DSN 2003).



physics.statistics.calc_consecutive_detection_frames(
    per_frame_detection,
    all_miss_probability,
)
Consecutive frames a person must be in view before detection may be counted on.
Equation: N = ceil( ln p_miss / ln(1 - p_frame) )
the fewest frames for which the chance of missing the person in every one, (1 - p_frame)^N, is at most all_miss_probability, with misses independent from frame to frame (the best case; correlated misses need more frames). A tolerance of 1e-12 keeps an exact ratio from rounding up.



physics.statistics.calc_cross_entropy_exponential_proposal(
    threshold,
    operational_mean,
    elite_share,
)
Expected (large-sample) cross-entropy iteration for an exponential tail.
From q_0 = p = Exp(m0), each round sets the level to the (1 - beta) quantile of the current proposal, level = -m_k ln(beta) (capped at the threshold), and refits the proposal mean to the likelihood-weighted elite draws; for this family that is E_p[D | D > level] = level + m0. Stops when the level reaches the threshold, so the final mean is threshold + m0.
Returns a dict with levels (list, in the units of threshold), n_levels, and proposal_mean.
Source: Rubinstein and Kroese, The Cross-Entropy Method (Springer, 2004), multilevel rare-event algorithm; the exponential refit is in closed form.



physics.statistics.calc_dagger_cost_bound(
    horizon_steps,
    per_step_error,
    recoverability=1.0,
)
Worst-case excess cost with expert labels on learner states: u S eps.
Ross, Gordon, and Bagnell (2011), Theorem 3.2: linear in the horizon while the recoverability constant u stays bounded.



physics.statistics.calc_effective_sample_size(n_records, lag1_correlation)
Effective number of independent samples in n_records of an AR(1) series.
N_eff = N (1 - rho) / (1 + rho) for estimating the mean of a series whose adjacent records have lag-one correlation rho (Thiebaux and Zwiers 1984).



physics.statistics.calc_equal_n_for_z(rate_a, rate_b, z_critical)
Per-group sample size at which the pooled two-proportion z of a fixed gap reaches z_critical.
With equal groups, z = gap / sqrt(2 p (1 - p) / n), so n = 2 p (1 - p) (z_critical / gap)^2 with p the mean of the two rates.



physics.statistics.calc_expected_calibration_error(bins)
Expected calibration error of binned predictions: sum |B_i| / n * |acc_i - conf_i|.
bins is a sequence of (count, confidence, accuracy); the weight of each bin is its share of the predictions (Pakdaman Naeini et al. 2015; Guo et al. 2017, eq. 3).



physics.statistics.calc_exponential_decay_rate(initial, later, elapsed)
Rate gamma of A(t) = A0 exp(-gamma t) through two readings: gamma = ln(A0 / A1) / t. elapsed may be a Quantity (the rate is then per its unit) or a plain number.



physics.statistics.calc_fisher_exact_two_sided(a, b, c, d)
Two-sided Fisher exact p for the 2x2 table [[a, b], [c, d]] (rows are the two arms).
Sums the hypergeometric probabilities of every table with the observed margins that is no more probable than the observed one. Source: Fisher, Statistical Methods for Research Workers (1934 ed.), sec. 21.02.



physics.statistics.calc_gaussian_kl(mean_p, sd_p, mean_q, sd_q)
KL divergence KL(P || Q) between two normal distributions, in nats.



physics.statistics.calc_gaussian_kl_terms(mean_p, sd_p, mean_q, sd_q)
The two terms of KL(P || Q) for normals P and Q.
KL = ln(sd_q / sd_p) + (sd_p^2 + (mean_p - mean_q)^2) / (2 sd_q^2) - 1/2. Returns (log_term, ratio_numerator, ratio_denominator) so a worked example can show each piece; calc_gaussian_kl adds them.



physics.statistics.calc_importance_sampling_exponential(
    threshold,
    operational_mean,
    proposal_mean,
)
Importance-sampling statistics for an exponential tail with an exponential proposal.
Operational model p = Exp(mean m0), failure when D > gamma, proposal q = Exp(mean m_q) with likelihood ratio w = p/q. Writing lam = 1/m0 and eta = 1/m_q (eta < 2 lam so the second moment is finite):
P_F                 = exp(-lam gamma)
E_q[w^2 1{D>gamma}] = lam^2 / (eta (2 lam - eta)) * exp(-(2 lam - eta) gamma)
relative variance   = E_q[w^2 1{D>gamma}] / P_F^2 - 1      (per draw)
ESS per draw        = E_q[w]^2 / E_q[w^2] = eta (2 lam - eta) / lam^2
P_q(D > gamma)      = exp(-eta gamma)
Draws for a relative standard error r are relative_variance / r**2. threshold, operational_mean, and proposal_mean are Pint quantities of one dimension (or plain floats in one unit).
Source: likelihood-ratio estimator, its second moment, and the effective sample size (sum w)^2 / sum w^2 from Owen 2013, ch. 9; the exponential closed forms follow by integrating those expressions.



physics.statistics.calc_jensen_shannon_divergence(p, q)
Jensen-Shannon divergence between two aligned distributions, in nats.
JS = KL(p || m) / 2 + KL(q || m) / 2 with m = (p + q) / 2. It is symmetric and bounded by ln 2, which two distributions with disjoint support reach. Source: Lin, “Divergence Measures Based on the Shannon Entropy,” IEEE Trans. Inf. Theory 37(1), 1991.



physics.statistics.calc_ks_coefficient(significance)
Large-sample two-sample K-S coefficient c(alpha) = sqrt(-ln(alpha / 2) / 2).
About 1.36 at 0.05 (Ops.Monitoring.KsTestCoefficient) and 1.63 at 0.01; calc_ks_critical_value scales it by the two sample sizes.



physics.statistics.calc_ks_critical_value(coefficient, n_reference, n_current)
Large-sample two-sample Kolmogorov-Smirnov critical value.
D_crit = c * sqrt((n_0 + n_t) / (n_0 * n_t)), where c is the coefficient for the chosen significance level (1.36 at 0.05, Ops.Monitoring.KsTestCoefficient).



physics.statistics.calc_ks_normal_location_shift(shift_sd)
K-S distance between two equal-variance normals whose means differ by shift_sd sds.
The CDF gap is largest midway between the means: 2 * Phi(shift_sd / 2) - 1, which equals erf(shift_sd / (2 * sqrt(2))).



physics.statistics.calc_linf_corner_l2(linf_budget, coordinates)
Euclidean length of a corner of the l-infinity ball of radius linf_budget in coordinates dimensions.



physics.statistics.calc_mcnemar_exact_two_sided(first_only, second_only)
Exact two-sided McNemar p from the discordant counts (McNemar 1947).
Conditional on d = first_only + second_only discordant pairs, wins are Binomial(d, 1/2) under equal marginals: p = min(1, 2 sum_{j <= min(b, c)} C(d, j) 2^-d); 1 when d = 0.



physics.statistics.calc_mcnemar_max_discordant(net_gap, critical)
Largest disagreement count b + c at which McNemar’s statistic still exceeds critical.
The statistic (no continuity correction) is (b - c)^2 / (b + c); with the net gap b - c fixed, it exceeds the 1-dof chi-square critical value only when b + c <= floor(gap^2 / critical) (McNemar 1947).



physics.statistics.calc_mean_half_width(sd, n_samples, confidence)
Half-width of a confidence interval on a mean of n_samples values: t_{n-1} sd / sqrt(n).



physics.statistics.calc_monte_carlo_sample_size(
    failure_probability,
    relative_error,
)
Plain Monte Carlo draws needed to estimate a probability to a relative error.
Equation: N = (1 - p) / (p * r^2)
The binomial estimator p_hat = k/N has relative standard error sqrt((1 - p) / (N p)); solving for N at a target r gives the count.
Source: Owen, Monte Carlo Theory, Methods and Examples (2013): the variance of a sample mean of Bernoulli draws, as used for rare events in ch. 9.



physics.statistics.calc_multilegged_confidence(leg_confidences)
Confidence in a claim supported by independent legs, any one of which suffices.
Equation: P(claim) = 1 - prod_i (1 - p_i)
Holds only if the legs fail independently; common-cause failure collapses the legs back into a conjunction.
Source: Bloomfield and Littlewood 2003 (DSN), multi-legged arguments under the independence assumption.



physics.statistics.calc_newcombe_paired_difference(
    both,
    first_only,
    second_only,
    neither,
    z_critical,
)
Paired difference of two acceptance rates with Newcombe’s method-10 interval (Newcombe 1998).
The four cells count the tasks both configurations accept, only the first, only the second, and neither. Returns (delta, low, high) for the first configuration’s rate minus the second’s. Each marginal Wilson interval is combined through the continuity-corrected phi of the 2x2 table, so positive within-pair dependence narrows the interval.



physics.statistics.calc_noncentral_gate_detection(gate, dof, noncentrality)
Probability that a biased innovation’s NIS exceeds gate (added 2026-10-20).
A bias b in an innovation of variance S makes its NIS noncentral chi-square with noncentrality b^2 / S, so its mean is dof + b^2 / S; a single-update gate catches it only with this probability.
Source: Bar-Shalom, Li, and Kirubarajan (2001), Sec. 1.4.17 (noncentral chi-square) and Sec. 5.4.



physics.statistics.calc_one_proportion_sample_size(
    null_rate,
    alternative_rate,
    z_alpha,
    z_beta,
)
Outcomes a one-sample binomial test needs to tell alternative_rate from null_rate.
Normal approximation with the variance of each hypothesis on its own side: n = ((z_alpha sqrt(p0 (1 - p0)) + z_beta sqrt(p1 (1 - p1))) / (p0 - p1))^2. The count grows as one over the squared gap, so halving the gap needs about four times the outcomes.



physics.statistics.calc_optimal_exponential_proposal_mean(
    threshold,
    operational_mean,
)
Mean of the exponential proposal that minimizes importance-sampling variance.
Minimizing the second moment of calc_importance_sampling_exponential over eta gives the root below 2 lam of
gamma eta^2 - (2 + 2 lam gamma) eta + 2 lam = 0,
and the proposal mean is 1/eta. Returned in the units of threshold.
Source: first-order condition on the exponential second moment (Owen 2013, ch. 9, exponential tilting of a light-tailed tail).



physics.statistics.calc_paired_difference_variance(
    discordant_fraction,
    difference,
)
Per-pair variance of a paired candidate-minus-baseline outcome in {-1, 0, +1}: d - delta^2.



physics.statistics.calc_poisson_exact_interval(events, alpha=0.05)
Exact (Garwood) two-sided 1 - alpha interval on a Poisson mean after events events.
Solves the Poisson tails P(N >= k) = alpha/2 (lower) and P(N <= k) = alpha/2 (upper) by bisection. Divide by the exposure to get a rate interval. Source: Garwood, “Fiducial Limits for the Poisson Distribution,” Biometrika 28(3/4), 1936.



physics.statistics.calc_poisson_mean_for_reserve(reserve, target, iterations=60)
Largest Poisson mean at which reserve still holds P(N >= reserve) below target.
Bisection on the tail, which rises monotonically with the mean.



physics.statistics.calc_poisson_reserve(mean, target)
Smallest reserve s whose Poisson tail P(N >= s) is below target.



physics.statistics.calc_poisson_tail(mean, at_least)
P(N >= s) for N ~ Poisson(mean): 1 - sum_{k<s} e^-m m^k / k!.
The chance that at least s events fall in an interval whose expected count is mean; 1 for s <= 0. A pool with s standby instances and a constant replenishment lead time misses a request exactly when at least s earlier replacements are still outstanding.



physics.statistics.calc_population_stability_index(
    expected,
    actual,
    epsilon=1e-12,
)
Population Stability Index (PSI) between two aligned distributions.
Measures distribution drift between a reference (“expected”) and an observed (“actual”) binned distribution: PSI = sum_i (actual_i - expected_i) * ln(actual_i / expected_i) (the symmetrized KL divergence). Interpretation thresholds live in Ops.Monitoring (the single source of truth the book follows: 0.10 warn / 0.20 review / 0.25 critical) — do not restate bands here.











Name
Type
Description
Default




expected
sequence of float
Bin probabilities (dimensionless, each summing to ~1), aligned bin-for-bin and of equal length.
required


actual
sequence of float
Bin probabilities (dimensionless, each summing to ~1), aligned bin-for-bin and of equal length.
required


epsilon
float
Floor applied to every bin to avoid log(0) / division by zero when a bin is empty.
1e-12














Name
Type
Description





float
PSI value (dimensionless, >= 0; 0 means identical distributions).







physics.statistics.calc_proportion_gap_interval(
    rate_a,
    rate_b,
    n_a,
    n_b,
    z_critical,
)
Normal-approximation interval of a gap rate_a - rate_b (unpooled standard error).
Returns (low, high): the gap minus and plus z_critical standard errors, se = sqrt(p_a (1 - p_a) / n_a + p_b (1 - p_b) / n_b).



physics.statistics.calc_proportion_gap_se(rate_a, rate_b, n_a, n_b)
Unpooled standard error of a gap rate_a - rate_b between two independent groups (added 2026-10-20).
se = sqrt(p_a (1 - p_a) / n_a + p_b (1 - p_b) / n_b).



physics.statistics.calc_proportion_half_width(rate, n_samples, z_critical)
Normal-approximation half-width of a proportion from n_samples independent draws: z sqrt(p (1 - p) / n).



physics.statistics.calc_sample_collection_time(
    samples,
    request_rate,
    traffic_share,
)
Time for a traffic slice to collect samples observations (added 2026-10-20).
A canary stage that receives traffic_share of request_rate gathers its planned guardrail sample in t = n / (r p).



physics.statistics.calc_samples_for_half_width(rate, half_width, z_critical)
Independent draws for a normal-approximation half-width at rate: ceil(z^2 p (1 - p) / h^2).



physics.statistics.calc_samples_per_arm_for_difference(
    sd,
    difference,
    z_alpha,
    z_beta,
)
Samples per arm for a two-sided two-sample test of a mean difference: 2 (z_a + z_b)^2 sd^2 / d^2.
The normal-approximation power formula; z_alpha is the two-sided critical value (1.96 at 95 percent) and z_beta the power quantile (0.84 at 80 percent power). Not rounded up.



physics.statistics.calc_smoothing_radius(noise_sd, top_class_probability)
Binary randomized-smoothing certified l2 radius sigma * Phi^-1(p_A) (Cohen et al. 2019).



physics.statistics.calc_spearman_rank_correlation(xs, ys)
Spearman’s rank correlation: Pearson correlation of the average ranks (ties share a rank).



physics.statistics.calc_split_conformal_min_count(alpha)
Fewest calibration scores for which the split-conformal rank exists (added 2026-10-20).
The rank ceil((n + 1)(1 - alpha)) must not exceed n, which holds from n = ceil((1 - alpha) / alpha).



physics.statistics.calc_split_conformal_rank(calibration_count, alpha)
Rank of the sorted calibration score that bounds new scores at level 1 - alpha (added 2026-10-20).
Split conformal prediction takes the ceil((n + 1)(1 - alpha))-th smallest of n exchangeable calibration scores; a new score exceeds it with probability at most alpha. A rank above n means the calibration set is too small to state the bound.
Source: Angelopoulos and Bates, “Conformal Prediction: A Gentle Introduction,” Found. Trends Mach. Learn. 16(4), 2023, Sec. 1.



physics.statistics.calc_sprt_boundaries(alpha, beta)
Wald’s accept and reject boundaries on the log-likelihood ratio: ln((1-b)/a), ln(b/(1-a)).
alpha is the allowed false acceptance of H1 under H0 and beta the allowed false rejection of H1 under H1 (Wald 1945).



physics.statistics.calc_sprt_expected_samples(
    upper,
    lower,
    drift,
    upper_probability,
)
Wald’s expected stopping sample count, neglecting overshoot.
The walk ends at upper with probability upper_probability and at lower otherwise; dividing the expected terminal log-likelihood by the expected step drift gives E[N] (Wald 1945, average sample number).



physics.statistics.calc_sprt_increments(p_unacceptable, p_acceptable)
Wald SPRT log-likelihood increments per success and per failure, failure-probability convention.
With per-trial failure probability p0 under H0 (unacceptable) and p1 under H1 (acceptable), a success adds ln((1 - p1)/(1 - p0)) and a failure adds ln(p1/p0) to the log-likelihood ratio of H1 over H0. Source: Wald, “Sequential Tests of Statistical Hypotheses,” Ann. Math. Statist. 16(2), 1945.



physics.statistics.calc_standard_error(sd, n_samples)
Standard error of a mean of n_samples independent values with spread sd: sd / sqrt(n).



physics.statistics.calc_t_critical(degrees_of_freedom, confidence)
Two-sided Student t critical value: the (1 + confidence) / 2 quantile (2.78 at 4 dof, 0.95).
Non-integer degrees of freedom (Welch-Satterthwaite) are allowed.



physics.statistics.calc_task_averaged_variance(
    between_task_variance,
    within_task_variance,
    tasks,
    runs_per_task,
)
Variance of a task-averaged acceptance estimate: sigma_task^2 / N + sigma_run^2 / (N r).
Tasks are sampled independently and runs are independent given the task; more runs shrink only the second term, more tasks shrink both.



physics.statistics.calc_two_proportion_detectable_lift(
    baseline_rate,
    n_per_variant,
    z_alpha=1.96,
    z_beta=0.84,
)
Smallest absolute lift a two-arm test with n_per_variant per arm can detect.
The common-variance sample-size formula of calc_two_proportion_sample_size solved for the effect: delta = sqrt(2 (z_alpha + z_beta)^2 p (1 - p) / n).



physics.statistics.calc_two_proportion_sample_size(
    baseline_rate,
    detectable_lift,
    z_alpha=1.96,
    z_beta=0.84,
    pooled=False,
)
Per-arm sample size for a two-proportion A/B test.
Standard normal-approximation power formula: n = 2 * (z_alpha + z_beta)^2 * p(1-p) / delta^2, using the baseline rate’s variance for both arms (a common simplification valid for small lifts). Defaults correspond to a two-sided 5% significance level (z = 1.96) and 80% power (z = 0.84).











Name
Type
Description
Default




baseline_rate
float
Control-arm conversion rate p in (0, 1).
required


detectable_lift
float
Minimum absolute difference in rates to detect (same 0-1 scale as baseline_rate, e.g. 0.01 for one percentage point). Must be > 0.
required


z_alpha
float
Normal quantile for the significance level (1.96 = two-sided 0.05).
1.96


z_beta
float
Normal quantile for power (0.84 = 80% power).
0.84


pooled
bool
When True, use the pooled two-proportion form, which carries the variance of both arms rather than reusing the baseline’s for each: n = (z_alpha * sqrt(2 * p_bar * q_bar)        + z_beta * sqrt(p1*q1 + p2*q2))^2 / delta^2 where p_bar is the mean of the two rates. This is the textbook form and the one the book’s own appendix displays. It is not the default because the simplified form above is already in use and its results are quoted in print; pass pooled=True where the pooled form is the one being taught.
False














Name
Type
Description





float
Required sample size per arm (unrounded; callers should ceil).







physics.statistics.calc_two_proportion_z(rate_a, rate_b, n_a, n_b)
Pooled two-proportion z statistic for an observed gap rate_a - rate_b.
z = (p_a - p_b) / sqrt(p (1 - p) (1/n_a + 1/n_b)) with the pooled rate p = (n_a p_a + n_b p_b) / (n_a + n_b), the null hypothesis that both groups share one rate.



physics.statistics.calc_wald_interval(successes, trials, z_critical)
Wald interval for a binomial proportion: p_hat +/- z sqrt(p_hat (1 - p_hat) / n).
Not clipped to [0, 1], so near the boundaries it shows the impossible endpoints and the zero width at x = 0 or x = n that disqualify it (Brown, Cai, and DasGupta 2001).



physics.statistics.calc_welch_interval(
    mean_a,
    sd_a,
    n_a,
    mean_b,
    sd_b,
    n_b,
    confidence,
)
Welch’s interval on mean_a - mean_b for two samples with unequal spreads (Welch 1947).
se = sqrt(s_a^2 / n_a + s_b^2 / n_b); the Welch-Satterthwaite degrees of freedom are se^4 / ((s_a^2/n_a)^2 / (n_a - 1) + (s_b^2/n_b)^2 / (n_b - 1)). Returns dict(difference, se, dof, t, low, high).



physics.statistics.calc_wilson_clean_runs(target_upper, z)
Fewest consecutive clean runs whose Wilson upper limit on the failure rate falls below target_upper.
With zero failures in n runs the upper limit is z^2 / (n + z^2), which is below t once n > z^2 (1 - t) / t.



physics.statistics.calc_wilson_interval(successes, trials, z_critical)
Wilson score interval for a binomial proportion (Wilson 1927), clipped to [0, 1].
center = (x + z^2/2) / (n + z^2)
half   = z / (n + z^2) * sqrt(x (n - x) / n + z^2 / 4)
The variance uses the hypothesized rate, so the interval keeps a nonzero width at x = 0 and x = n and never leaves [0, 1].



physics.statistics.calc_within_task_variance(mean_rate, between_task_variance)
Mean within-task run variance E[p_i (1 - p_i)] = mean (1 - mean) - Var(p_i).



physics.statistics.fit_exponential_growth(xs, ys, period=1.0)
Least-squares fit of log10(y) on x; growth factor per period of x.
Returns (factor, slope, intercept) where log10(y) = intercept + slope * x and factor = 10 ** (slope * period). Trend lines on log-scale technology plots (compute, memory bandwidth, interconnect against year) are this fit.

title: engine.solvers.estimation
text:
engine.solvers.estimation
Spatial-memory solvers: state estimation, estimator consistency, drift, and belief expiry (added 2026-10-20).
Domain implementations behind mlsysim.solvers. The equations live in physics/robotics/estimation.py, physics/robotics/perception.py, physics/robotics/sensing.py, and physics/statistics.py; these models compose them for one stated estimator, sensor, benchmark, or belief, so a chapter, a slide deck, and a lab read the same arithmetic.





Name
Description




BeliefExpiryModel
A belief’s error bound E(dt) = E_0 + v dt + a dt^2 / 2, its invalidation horizon, and an admission check.


EpochGapModel
Travel across the gap between two acquisition epochs, speed x \|t2 - t1\|.


EstimatorConsistencyModel
The band a campaign’s mean NEES or NIS must fall in, and what single-update gates catch.


FreeSpaceExpiryModel
Occluded free space eroding inward at the approach speed v_h, ahead and abreast of an occluder.


FrozenTransformModel
A last transform republished every republish_period with fresh stamps while the object moves.


InertialCoastModel
An IMU integrated open loop for duration, with the heading offset seen at target_range.


OdometryDriftModel
A benchmark’s return error over its path as a drift rate, before and after calibration.


RangeFusionModel
One scalar predict and two updates of a range, and the same second update misdated.


ReplayBufferModel
Slots of a rewind buffer sampled at sample_rate that reach back horizon: ceil(horizon / dt).


SensorBiasDriftModel
A bias drifting at drift_rate for span under a steady reading: the true value is the reading less the shift.


StaleTransformModel
A cached sensor-to-target edge, one interval old, composed with the current wrist pose.





engine.solvers.estimation.BeliefExpiryModel()
A belief’s error bound E(dt) = E_0 + v dt + a dt^2 / 2, its invalidation horizon, and an admission check.
The horizon is calc_quadratic_invalidation_horizon; dropping the acceleration term gives the constant-velocity horizon, at which the true bound has already overrun the tolerance. With use_age, the consumer’s age bound is use_age + age_bound (the clock-conversion bound), and the belief is admitted if the error there is within tolerance; the latest admissible use age is the horizon less age_bound.



engine.solvers.estimation.EpochGapModel()
Travel across the gap between two acquisition epochs, speed x |t2 - t1|.
With separation, the slack is the separation less the committed terms (localization bound and protective clearance), which the travel across the gap must fit inside.



engine.solvers.estimation.EstimatorConsistencyModel()
The band a campaign’s mean NEES or NIS must fall in, and what single-update gates catch.
calc_chi2_mean_band gives the band for runs statistics of dimension dimension; each gate is calc_chi2_gate at its confidence, and a biased update with mean NIS nis_expected exceeds it with calc_noncentral_gate_detection (noncentrality nis_expected - dimension).



engine.solvers.estimation.FreeSpaceExpiryModel()
Occluded free space eroding inward at the approach speed v_h, ahead and abreast of an occluder.
Each horizon is calc_free_space_expiry; the observation age spends part of it before memory receives the frame. A walker approaching during a stop at speed covers v_h (tau_delay + v / a_brake).



engine.solvers.estimation.FrozenTransformModel()
A last transform republished every republish_period with fresh stamps while the object moves.
Every copy passes a publish-time freshness_threshold; the object has moved speed x window from the frozen pose.



engine.solvers.estimation.InertialCoastModel()
An IMU integrated open loop for duration, with the heading offset seen at target_range.
calc_inertial_coast_errors gives the four terms; the heading offset moves a point at range sideways by calc_lever_arm_error. The position offset is priced against reference (a localization bound).



engine.solvers.estimation.OdometryDriftModel()
A benchmark’s return error over its path as a drift rate, before and after calibration.
The rate eps = E / L spends a bound delta after delta / eps of travel, which takes delta / (eps v) at the operating speed; over a segment of length s the error is eps s.



engine.solvers.estimation.RangeFusionModel()
One scalar predict and two updates of a range, and the same second update misdated.
Prediction adds (sigma_v dt)^2; each update applies calc_scalar_kalman_update. A reading paired with the wrong pose is off by misdating_bias; the update moves the estimate g b while the reported spread, which uses only the modeled noise, is unchanged. Its innovation’s NIS has mean 1 + b^2 / S. comparison_scale reruns the second update with that sensor’s spread scaled.



engine.solvers.estimation.ReplayBufferModel()
Slots of a rewind buffer sampled at sample_rate that reach back horizon: ceil(horizon / dt).



engine.solvers.estimation.SensorBiasDriftModel()
A bias drifting at drift_rate for span under a steady reading: the true value is the reading less the shift.



engine.solvers.estimation.StaleTransformModel()
A cached sensor-to-target edge, one interval old, composed with the current wrist pose.
The finger error is the initial error, plus the unobserved drift over the interval v dt, plus the lever-arm swing l omega dt of the rotation the cached edge never saw. Composing the edge with the wrist pose of its own epoch removes the lever term and leaves the belief’s own bound.

A benchmark’s return error over its path as a drift rate, before and after calibration.
The rate eps = E / L spends a bound delta after delta / eps of travel, which takes delta / (eps v) at the operating speed; over a segment of length s the error is eps s.



engine.solvers.estimation.RangeFusionModel()
One scalar predict and two updates of a range, and the same second update misdated.
Prediction adds (sigma_v dt)^2; each update applies calc_scalar_kalman_update. A reading paired with the wrong pose is off by misdating_bias; the update moves the estimate g b while the reported spread, which uses only the modeled noise, is unchanged. Its innovation’s NIS has mean 1 + b^2 / S. comparison_scale reruns the second update with that sensor’s spread scaled.



engine.solvers.estimation.ReplayBufferModel()
Slots of a rewind buffer sampled at sample_rate that reach back horizon: ceil(horizon / dt).



engine.solvers.estimation.SensorBiasDriftModel()
A bias drifting at drift_rate for span under a steady reading: the true value is the reading less the shift.



engine.solvers.estimation.StaleTransformModel()
A cached sensor-to-target edge, one interval old, composed with the current wrist pose.
The finger error is the initial error, plus the unobserved drift over the interval v dt, plus the lever-arm swing l omega dt of the rotation the cached edge never saw. Composing the edge with the wrist pose of its own epoch removes the lever term and leaves the belief’s own bound.

physics.performance.calc_partial_slowdown_stretch(stall_fraction, slowdown)
Stretch of a task when only a fraction of its time is slowed down.
Equation: stretch = (1 - f) + f * S
Amdahl’s law read as a slowdown: a fraction f of the unloaded time (for example, time stalled on shared-cache misses) runs S times slower under interference while the rest is unchanged. The loaded time is t_unloaded * stretch. Equal to 1 / calc_amdahls_speedup(f, 1/S).
Source: Amdahl, “Validity of the single processor approach to achieving large scale computing capabilities,” AFIPS Spring Joint Computer Conference, 1967 (fixed-fraction model, applied to a slowdown).

1

physics.performance.calc_stall_share_breakeven(allowed_stretch, slowdown)
Largest slowed fraction of a task that keeps it within an allowed stretch.
Equation: f_max = (C / t_unloaded - 1) / (S - 1)
The inverse of calc_partial_slowdown_stretch: with a budget C (a declared WCET or deadline) and unloaded time t_unloaded, the allowed stretch is C / t_unloaded; a slowed share above f_max crosses the budget. Capped at 1 (the whole task may be slowed).

physics.performance.calc_universal_scalability_law(n, sigma, kappa)
Universal Scalability Law (Gunther, 1993).
Calculates relative system throughput / speedup C(N) under concurrency N, accounting for both serialization contention (sigma) and coherency crosstalk / coordination overhead (kappa).

title: engine.solvers.facility
text:
engine.solvers.facility
Facility solvers: power transients, coolant flow, and outage cost.
Domain implementations behind mlsysim.solvers (the public import path, derived from engine.solvers.__init__); kept per-domain so the logic stays reviewable.





Name
Description




CoolantFlowModel
Coolant flow that carries a heat load at a stated temperature rise.


OutageCostModel
Idle cost of a failure domain going down during a synchronous job.


PowerTransientModel
One accelerator’s load step and the ramp a synchronized cluster produces.





engine.solvers.facility.CoolantFlowModel()
Coolant flow that carries a heat load at a stated temperature rise.
m_dot = Q / (c_p dT), then volume flow from the coolant’s density. Water’s specific heat is about four times air’s and its density about 830 times, so it carries the same heat in thousands of times less volume.



engine.solvers.facility.OutageCostModel()
Idle cost of a failure domain going down during a synchronous job.
The direct cost counts only the devices in the failed domain. A synchronous job that cannot continue idles every device, and rolling back to the last checkpoint adds the lost work to the repair window.



engine.solvers.facility.PowerTransientModel()
One accelerator’s load step and the ramp a synchronized cluster produces.
When a collective barrier releases every device from communication into dense arithmetic, each one steps from its communication-phase power toward its design power at once. On one device’s core rail the step is a current change dP / V, and the board loop’s inductance turns a fast edge into a voltage droop L dI/dt. Across the cluster the same step, aligned by the barrier, is a power ramp the facility supplies must follow.

engine.solvers.training.CheckpointModel()
Analyzes the storage constraints and I/O burst penalties of saving model states.
Training massive models requires saving hundreds of gigabytes (Weights + Optimizer States) to persistent storage. This model calculates the time spent blocked on I/O, subtracting from the cluster’s Model FLOPs Utilization.

engine.solvers.training.TrainingMemoryModel()
Decomposes per-accelerator training memory into teachable components.
This model answers a different question than SingleNodeModel. Roofline feasibility asks whether a workload’s inference weights fit; training feasibility must also account for gradients, optimizer state, activations, and communication buffers. The accounting follows the common mixed-precision state breakdown used by Megatron-LM and ZeRO.
Literature Source: 1. Shoeybi et al. (2019), “Megatron-LM” (tensor/pipeline parallel state). 2. Rajbhandari et al. (2020), “ZeRO” (data-parallel state sharding). 3. Korthikanti et al. (2023), activation recomputation accounting.
Formula contract: - parameter states are sharded by TP * PP * EP before ZeRO sharding. - ZeRO-1 shards optimizer state, ZeRO-2 also shards gradients, and ZeRO-3 also shards weights across DP. - activation memory is based on local microbatch, layers per pipeline stage, hidden dimension, and the actual bytes per element for the precision.





Name
Description




solve
Estimate per-accelerator training memory.





engine.solvers.training.TrainingMemoryModel.solve(
    model,
    hardware,
    batch_size,
    seq_len=2048,
    precision='fp16',
    optimizer='adam',
    activation_checkpointing='selective',
    tp_size=1,
    pp_size=1,
    dp_size=1,
    ep_size=1,
    zero_stage=0,
    gradient_accumulation_steps=1,
    trainable_fraction=1.0,
    communication_buffer_fraction=0.05,
    sequence_parallel=True,
)
Estimate per-accelerator training memory.
batch_size is the global batch. The activation term uses the local microbatch implied by data parallelism and gradient accumulation. Model states are sharded by tensor, pipeline, and expert parallelism first; ZeRO then shards optimizer, gradient, and parameter states across the data-parallel group according to its stage.
With tp_size > 1 and sequence_parallel (the Megatron-LM recipe Korthikanti et al. 2023 evaluate), every stored activation is split across the tensor-parallel group, so the activation term divides by tp_size (their Table 2). Without sequence parallelism the LayerNorm and dropout activations stay replicated; that case keeps the unsharded activation term as a conservative upper bound.





engine.solvers.training.TrainingRunModel()
Wall-clock time of a training run, from peak throughput to delivered time.
The chain starts from the 6PD training FLOPs at every device’s peak, divides by the local compute efficiency (the compute-only baseline), then by the scaling efficiency (communication and pipeline bubbles), then multiplies by each operational overhead in order (checkpointing, failures and restarts, maintenance), each relative to the subtotal before it.
Literature Source: 1. Kaplan et al. (2020) and Hoffmann et al. (2022), the 6PD rule. 2. Narayanan et al. (2021), scaling efficiency at cluster scale.



engine.solvers.training.TrainingStateModel()
Persistent mixed-precision Adam state and how parallelism shards it.
Per parameter: FP16 weights and gradients (2 B each), FP32 master weights (4 B), and two FP32 Adam moments (4 B each), 16 B in all. Tensor parallelism splits every term across the TP group; ZeRO-style sharding further splits the optimizer moments across the data-parallel replicas. Activations are a stated total, not derived (they depend on sequence length, microbatch, and recomputation).
Literature Source: 1. Rajbhandari et al. (2020), “ZeRO” (16 B/param accounting, sharding). 2. Shoeybi et al. (2019), “Megatron-LM” (tensor parallelism).

title: models.types.Workload
text:
models.types.Workload()
Layer A (Workload Demand): Base representation of an ML model or task.
A Workload defines the computational requirements of a task without any knowledge of the hardware it will run on. It must implement lower() to project its architectural definition down into a ComputationGraph.
inference_flops semantics — the unit of work DIFFERS BY MODEL FAMILY (documented 2026-06-06; the field is dimensioned only as flop, so the family convention is the contract):

Autoregressive LMs (TransformerWorkload decoder-only, SparseTransformerWorkload): FLOPs per generated token, following the 2 x params convention — 2 x TOTAL params for dense models, 2 x ACTIVE params for MoE.
Encoder models (BERT-family): FLOPs per sequence at the reference sequence length recorded in the entry’s provenance (BERT-Base: 22 GFLOP at seq=128).
Vision / CNN / recommendation models: FLOPs per input (one image / one query forward pass).

NEVER compare inference_flops across families without normalizing — the magnitudes differ by orders of magnitude purely from the work unit.





Name
Description




lower
Lowers the workload into a hardware-agnostic computation graph.





models.types.Workload.lower(precision=BYTES_FP16)
Lowers the workload into a hardware-agnostic computation graph.
Default implementation uses parameters and inference_flops directly. Subclasses (Transformer, CNN, etc.) override this with architecture-specific lowering.

text:
solvers.FailureIntervalModel
solvers.FailureIntervalModel()
Interval between failures across identical, independent components.
With N components that each fail on average once per MTBF, some component fails on average every MTBF / N (the minimum of N exponentials). Over a run of a given length the expected failure count is the run length divided by that interval.
