title: physics.drivetrain
text:
physics.drivetrain
Braking-drive physics for a wheeled mobile base (Volume IV, added 2026-09-28, M6).
A credible deceleration is admissible only if three independent ceilings exceed it: tire-floor traction, tip-over about the leading support, and the torque the drives can deliver at their configured current limit. A fourth check asks whether the drive keeps current control at speed, which requires the motor’s back-EMF to stay below the bus.
Sources: Coulomb friction and the tipping moment balance are freshman rigid-body equilibrium (OpenStax, University Physics Volume 1, Secs. 6.2 and 12.2); the reflected rotating mass m_eff = m + sum(N^2 J / r^2) follows Lynch and Park, Modern Robotics (2017), Sec. 8.9.2; the brushless DC terminal equation V = e + I R is Krishnan, Permanent Magnet Synchronous and Brushless DC Motor Drives (CRC Press, 2010).





Name
Description




calc_braking_limits
Check a credible deceleration against the traction, tip-over, and drive-torque ceilings.


calc_drive_torque_deceleration_limit
Deceleration ceiling set by the torque the drives deliver at their current limit.


calc_drive_voltage_headroom
Terminal voltage a direct-drive wheel motor needs at speed, braking and driving.


calc_max_cg_height_ratio
Largest ratio h_cg / d at which a deceleration does not tip the machine.


calc_required_friction
Minimum friction coefficient that supports a deceleration on the braked wheels.


calc_tipover_deceleration_limit
Deceleration at which a braking machine starts to pitch over its leading support.


calc_traction_deceleration_limit
Deceleration ceiling set by tire-floor friction on the braked wheels.





physics.drivetrain.calc_braking_limits(
    mass,
    deceleration,
    *,
    wheel_torque_max,
    wheel_radius,
    n_driven_wheels,
    friction_coefficient,
    drive_load_share=1.0,
    rotating_equivalent_mass=None,
    cg_height=None,
    tip_arm=None,
)
Check a credible deceleration against the traction, tip-over, and drive-torque ceilings.
Each ceiling is computed by its own helper; the admissible deceleration is the smallest ceiling that could be computed. When the center-of-gravity geometry is unknown the tip-over ceiling is None and the result reports instead the largest h_cg / d the requested deceleration tolerates.
Source: see calc_traction_deceleration_limit, calc_tipover_deceleration_limit, and calc_drive_torque_deceleration_limit.










Name
Type
Description





dict
- “a_traction”, “a_torque”, “a_tip” (None if geometry unknown), “m_eff”, “force”, “mu_required”, “cg_ratio_max”, “a_admissible”, “binding”, and “passes” (True only if every computed ceiling meets the request and the tip-over ceiling was computed).







physics.drivetrain.calc_drive_torque_deceleration_limit(
    wheel_torque_max,
    wheel_radius,
    n_driven_wheels,
    mass,
    rotating_equivalent_mass=None,
)
Deceleration ceiling set by the torque the drives deliver at their current limit.
Equation: m_eff = m + sum_i J_i / r^2 (per wheel, reflected through N^2 if geared) a_torque = n * tau_wheel,max / (r * m_eff)
with tau_wheel,max = eta * N * K_t * I_max for a geared drive, or the hub motor’s torque at the current limit for direct drive (N = 1).
Source: Newton’s second law with the rotating parts reflected into the translational mass (Lynch and Park, Modern Robotics, 2017, Sec. 8.9.2).











Name
Type
Description
Default




wheel_torque_max
Quantity
Torque each driven wheel delivers at the configured current limit (N m).
required


wheel_radius
Quantity
Rolling radius r (m).
required


n_driven_wheels
int
Number of driven (braked) wheels.
required


mass
Quantity
Translating mass m (kg).
required


rotating_equivalent_mass
Quantity
Sum of N^2 J / r^2 over all rotating drive parts (kg). A sourced upper bound gives a lower bound on the deceleration.
None














Name
Type
Description





dict
- “force”: total retarding force at the floor (N) - “m_eff”: effective translational mass (kg) - “a_max”: deceleration ceiling (m/s^2)







physics.drivetrain.calc_drive_voltage_headroom(
    back_emf_constant,
    velocity,
    wheel_radius,
    bus_voltage,
    current,
    line_resistance,
)
Terminal voltage a direct-drive wheel motor needs at speed, braking and driving.
With two phases conducting, the line-to-line terminal equation is V = e + I R when driving and V = e - I R when braking (current opposes the back-EMF). The drive keeps current control while the voltage it must impose stays within the bus; if e itself exceeds the bus, the inverter’s diodes conduct and braking current is no longer controlled.
Equation: omega = v / r ; e = K_e * omega V_drive = e + I R ; V_brake = e - I R ; headroom = V_bus - e
Source: brushless DC motor terminal equation (Krishnan, Permanent Magnet Synchronous and Brushless DC Motor Drives, CRC Press, 2010).











Name
Type
Description
Default




back_emf_constant
Quantity
Line-to-line back-EMF per unit shaft speed (e.g. V/rpm).
required


velocity
Quantity
Ground speed (m/s).
required


wheel_radius
Quantity
Rolling radius (m).
required


bus_voltage
Quantity
DC bus voltage available to the drive (V).
required


current
Quantity
Phase current at which the check is made (A).
required


line_resistance
Quantity
Line-to-line winding resistance (ohm).
required














Name
Type
Description





dict
- “omega”: wheel speed (rpm) - “e_bemf”: back-EMF (V) - “v_drive”: terminal voltage to drive at this current (V) - “v_brake”: terminal voltage to brake at this current (V) - “headroom”: bus voltage minus back-EMF (V)







physics.drivetrain.calc_max_cg_height_ratio(deceleration)
Largest ratio h_cg / d at which a deceleration does not tip the machine.
Equation: (h_cg / d)_max = g / a
Source: inverse of calc_tipover_deceleration_limit.



physics.drivetrain.calc_required_friction(deceleration, drive_load_share=1.0)
Minimum friction coefficient that supports a deceleration on the braked wheels.
Equation: mu_min = a / (g * phi)
Source: inverse of calc_traction_deceleration_limit.



physics.drivetrain.calc_tipover_deceleration_limit(cg_height, tip_arm)
Deceleration at which a braking machine starts to pitch over its leading support.
The retarding force acts at the floor while inertia acts at the center of gravity, so braking pitches the body forward. It stays on the ground while the inertial moment m a h stays below the restoring moment m g d.
Equation: a_tip = g * d / h_cg
Source: moment balance about the tipping edge for a rigid body in static equilibrium (OpenStax, University Physics Volume 1, Sec. 12.2).











Name
Type
Description
Default




cg_height
Quantity
Height h_cg of the center of gravity above the floor (m).
required


tip_arm
Quantity
Horizontal distance d from the center of gravity to the leading support line (m), for the arm pose being checked.
required









Name
Type
Description





Quantity
Deceleration ceiling in m/s^2.







physics.drivetrain.calc_traction_deceleration_limit(
    friction_coefficient,
    drive_load_share=1.0,
)
Deceleration ceiling set by tire-floor friction on the braked wheels.
Equation: a_traction = mu * g * phi
where phi is the fraction of the machine’s weight carried by the braked (driven) wheels. Unbraked casters carry the rest and contribute no retarding force.
Source: Coulomb friction F <= mu N (OpenStax, University Physics Volume 1, Sec. 6.2, Eq. 6.2).











Name
Type
Description
Default




friction_coefficient
float
Tire-floor friction coefficient mu (dimensionless, > 0).
required


drive_load_share
float
Fraction phi of the weight on the braked wheels, in (0, 1].
1.0









Name
Type
Description





Quantity
Deceleration ceiling in m/s^2.

title: engine.solvers.interconnect
text:
engine.solvers.interconnect
Interconnect solvers: transfer bounds across link tiers, alpha-beta messages, bisection cuts, incast, and fits to measured collectives.
Domain implementations behind mlsysim.solvers (the public import path, derived from engine.solvers.__init__); kept per-domain so the logic stays reviewable.





Name
Description




AlphaBetaModel
Point-to-point message time under the alpha-beta model on several paths.


BisectionModel
A ring AllReduce whose every edge crosses the bisection, on a full and an oversubscribed cut.


CommunicationIntensityModel
Communication intensity of one data-parallel worker step against fabric balance.


GradientSyncModel
One data-parallel step: local compute, then a ring AllReduce of the gradients.


IncastModel
Many senders converge on one egress port (incast).


TensorParallelCommModel
Activation AllReduces of one tensor-parallel training step.


TransferLadderModel
Moves one payload over each tier of a bandwidth hierarchy.





engine.solvers.interconnect.AlphaBetaModel()
Point-to-point message time under the alpha-beta model on several paths.
Each message of n bytes pays a fixed startup alpha (NIC, switch hops, error correction, software) plus n / beta on the wire. The two terms are equal at n* = alpha * beta: below it a lower alpha helps, above it only a higher beta does.
Literature Source: Hockney (1994), “The communication challenge for MPP”.



engine.solvers.interconnect.BisectionModel()
A ring AllReduce whose every edge crosses the bisection, on a full and an oversubscribed cut.
With ranks placed alternately in the two halves, each of the N/2 ring edges in one direction crosses the cut and carries 2(N-1)/N times the per-device payload (ReduceScatter then AllGather). The cut carries N/2 links, divided by the oversubscription ratio. Only the communication fraction of the step stretches, so relative throughput is 1 / ((1 - f) + f r); the lost share of a cluster’s capital cost is its equivalent idle capacity. This placement is the worst case.



engine.solvers.interconnect.CommunicationIntensityModel()
Communication intensity of one data-parallel worker step against fabric balance.
CI is bytes sent over the network per FLOP done locally. The fabric’s balance point is link bandwidth over peak arithmetic rate: below it the step is set by compute, above it by the network.



engine.solvers.interconnect.GradientSyncModel()
One data-parallel step: local compute, then a ring AllReduce of the gradients.
Each worker sends about 2x the gradient bytes per step (the ring factor for large N). With no overlap the step is compute plus transfer, so the compute fraction shows how much of the step the accelerator works. Energy charges each transferred bit once at the fabric’s energy per bit.



engine.solvers.interconnect.IncastModel()
Many senders converge on one egress port (incast).
The offered load is the senders’ combined rate; the buffer fills at the offered load less what the egress drains, and a full buffer holds buffer / egress of waiting. The bandwidth-delay product is the data in flight on the egress link during one feedback round trip, which is what end-to-end congestion control must absorb before it can react.



engine.solvers.interconnect.TensorParallelCommModel()
Activation AllReduces of one tensor-parallel training step.
Each Transformer layer sums an activation-sized partial result across the tensor-parallel group once in the forward pass and once in the backward pass. A ring AllReduce over N devices moves 2(N-1)/N times the payload per device. The bound is bandwidth-only and assumes no overlap with the stated compute time, so the fractions are a diagnostic, not a forecast.
Literature Source: 1. Shoeybi et al. (2019), “Megatron-LM” (two AllReduces per layer per pass). 2. Patarasuk and Yuan (2009), ring AllReduce bandwidth factor.



engine.solvers.interconnect.TransferLadderModel()
Moves one payload over each tier of a bandwidth hierarchy.
The time on each tier is the bandwidth-only lower bound, bytes / bandwidth; per-message startup latency (the alpha term) is excluded. The ratios between tiers are the bandwidth staircase that decides where each kind of parallel traffic may run.
